selected_prs.title: feat(gateway): steer and edit a canonical queued prompt from Desktop
selected_prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Desktop's queue panel showed only Delete on a canonical (server-owned) queued prompt. The gateway had no verb that could steer or edit a queued admission. Composing `prompt.cancel` with `session.steer` or a resubmit takes two writes, and the drain can claim the row between them, so the prompt runs twice or is lost.

This adds two owner verbs that consume the still-queued admission inside the owner's own write transaction, and wires Desktop's Steer and Edit to them:

- **`prompt.steer_queued {admission_id}`** hands the queued text to the running turn's agent. It is served only once that turn has adopted its agent; otherwise it refuses `steer_unavailable` before the row is touched, so the prompt stays queued and runs in FIFO order. The row moves to a transfer state bound to the receiving claim and settles with that claim: `steered` when the turn completes and one of its drains consumed the text, `interrupted` when it ends any other way (never replayed). If the text never reached the turn (the turn ended before delivery, the text was still in the agent's steer buffer when the turn ended, or a hard stop dropped it unread), the row goes back to `queued` in its original FIFO place. The agent tracks each transfer by its admission id, never by its text, and a transfer never becomes the turn's leftover-steer follow-up. While the row is in transfer, `prompt.cancel` refuses it `stale_generation`, as it refuses a started row. Until it settles, its receipt reads `started`, and pending snapshots list it as `started` with `steering: true`. Refusals: `admission_started`, `session_idle`, `steer_unavailable`, `unsupported_control`, `not_found`.
- **`prompt.replace_queued {admission_id, submission_id, text, …}`** cancels the queued row inside the admission write of its successor. The successor joins the back of the FIFO under a new admission identity and is durably bound to the row it replaced. A retry naming the same old admission returns the same replacement; the same `submission_id` with a different old admission gets `admission_conflict`. Refusals: `admission_started`, `admission_conflict`, `queue_full`, `unsupported_control`, `not_found`.

Each pending row lists the queued-row verbs its owner serves (`controls`). Steer and Edit are Desktop-only for now: the TUI and the classic CLI get no queued-row steer/edit in this PR. Desktop shows Steer and Edit on a canonical row only when the row lists them, so an older gateway keeps Delete only. Canonical rows never get Next, because reordering would break the owner's one FIFO. Local rows are unchanged.

The change follows #106742: one FIFO and one writer, no client-side writer or queue state, and a named refusal when something can't be served. Queued admissions survive an owner restart and run FIFO exactly once. A steer still in transfer when its owner dies settles `interrupted` and is never replayed. A retry reuses the original identity.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (RT-35)
Refs #140208

Refs only, not Fixes: this has not been retested against a live Desktop build yet.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_runtime.py`:
  - `steer_session_input`: queued → terminal `steering`, bound to the running claim's `(owner_epoch, generation)`.
  - `settle_steer_transfers`: runs inside the claim's terminal write.
  - `revert_steer_input` (shares `_requeue_transfer` with settlement; `steer_replayed` is the one exact-retry check).
  - `recover_session_inputs` settles orphaned transfers as `interrupted`.
  - `admit_session_input(_replay_guard=…)`, plus `retire_replaced_input` / `check_replaced_input` (the replacement binding).
- `gateway/session_queued_controls.py`: both handlers, `queued_controls(authority, row)`, the transfer fence, and `pending_rows` (pending snapshots plus in-flight transfers).
- `agent/interrupt_control.py`: the steer buffer keeps each submission as a `(ticket, text)` part (`_pending_steer` stays their join). `steer(text, ticket=…)` tags a gateway transfer with its admission id, and `withdraw_steer(ticket)` settles exactly that submission. A drain marks the tickets it took as consumed and a hard stop marks them dropped; `_requeue_pending_steer` (now `requeue_drained_steer`) gives them back. `_drain_leftover_steer` hands back only ticketless steers.
- `agent/turn_finalizer.py`: the leftover-steer handoff uses `_drain_leftover_steer`, so a ticketed transfer stays buffered for its settlement (an agent without the method keeps the full drain).
- `hermes_state_runtime.cancel_session_input`: a row in transfer is refused `stale_generation`, like a started row.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`:
  - `steer_transfers` and `launch_sources`.
  - `_receipt` reads a transfer as `started`.
  - `submit(_replay_guard=…)`.
  - The drain publishes settled transfers.
- `gateway/session_settlement_recovery.py` / `gateway/session_results.py`: settlement, and the unknown-recovery fence, settle the claim's transfers in the same write.
- `gateway/session_controls.py`: registers the verbs. `prompt.submit` payload building moves to `submission()` so replace admits exactly what submit would.
- `tui_gateway/contracts/canonical_sessions.py` declares both verbs and `CanonicalPendingAdmission.controls` / `.steering`. `apps/shared` contracts regenerated.
- Desktop:
  - `pending-submissions` projects `controls`; a `steering` listing hides the card without raising the admission's rank, and cards the owner lists keep the owner's FIFO order, so a returned transfer is shown in its queue place.
  - `queue-panel` shows Edit/Steer only when they are served.
  - `queue-slot` routes Steer.
  - `use-composer-queue` keeps an edit until the owner answers it, settles a reply only against its own save, and keeps the replacement's identity while the outcome is unknown.
  - New notice strings in all 9 locales; `locales/_keys.desktop.json` regenerated.

### Design notes
- **Steer is a transfer, settled by the receiving claim.** Before the turn adopts its agent, a steer is refused, not latched. A latched text would be lost if agent construction then failed, while the row already reported `steered`. Main would have run that prompt, so refusing keeps it queued. The row is bound to the claim's generation in the database. Its final outcome is written in the same transaction that settles the claim, from an in-process record of whether the text reached that claim's agent. `agent.steer()` only buffers the text. The gateway tags each transfer with its admission id as a ticket, and the agent records per ticket whether a drain handed it to the turn. At settlement (the execution has returned, nothing can drain any more) the gateway asks the agent about each ticket (`withdraw_steer`). A transfer still buffered is taken out (other steers stay, whatever their text), and it counts as not delivered, as does one a hard stop dropped unread. The turn finalizer's leftover-steer handoff takes only ticketless steers (a `/steer` typed into the turn still becomes the next user turn), so a transfer never becomes a follow-up that a restart's drain could discard:
  - consumed by a drain + completed → `steered`;
  - consumed + anything else → `interrupted`;
  - not delivered, or withdrawn unconsumed → back to `queued`.
  The fence is dropped only on a definite refusal of the transfer write. After any other failure (a write can commit and still report one) the claim's settlement decides the row, and an exact retry delivers a committed transfer while its claim runs.
  Pending snapshots keep listing an in-flight transfer (`started`, `steering: true`, no controls). Desktop hides its card but never raises the admission's rank on that listing, so a transfer that goes back to `queued` gets its card back instead of staying retired.
  An owner restart before settlement makes it `interrupted`, matching #106742: a started admission that loses its owner is never replayed.
- **No storage write waits under the stream lock.** The transfer is registered, and later delivered, under the session's `event_stream.lock`. That is the lock the drain clears its executing stamp under, which makes the registration the fence against the claim's settlement. Every SQLite write runs outside the lock, as `session_settlement_recovery.commit_and_publish` already does. Reads under the lock (the cached launch-source lookup, the in-flight transfer rows) go through the lock-free WAL reader pool, as `_pending_rows` already does there. `SessionDB.get_session` is avoided because it flushes token counts, which is a write.
- **Replacement binding.** The successor's admission write records which admission it retired, keyed by the successor's durable identity (`state_meta`). The exact-replay path checks that record inside the same transaction. Ordinary `prompt.submit` payloads and digests are unchanged, so retries of admissions committed before this change replay as before.
- **Producer gating.** Controls are offered, and both verbs served, only for text-only rows of sessions launched from an interactive local surface: `cli`, `tui`, `gui`, `desktop` or `acp`, read from the session row's frozen launch source. `desktop` (the label a Desktop chat migrated from main keeps) counts as `gui`. Those observers settle `steered`/`cancelled`: viewers, and ACP's `end_turn`. Hosted-room (`bot_room`), cron, kanban and a2a producers expect a saved result for any outcome they don't name, so they are excluded and refused `unsupported_control`. API, bot-delivery and native messaging rows were already excluded by their payload envelopes.
- **Desktop edit.** Save keeps the edit open until `prompt.replace_queued` answers. Each save has its own token and remembers the exact edit it was made in, so a reply never settles a later edit (cancelled and reopened) and never overwrites text typed after Save. On a named refusal, or when the owner starts or removes the row mid-edit, the composer's current text stays as an unsent draft, followed by the draft it interrupted, with a short notice. A lost reply (no named refusal) leaves the outcome unknown: the edit stays open with a notice, and the next Save of the same text retries `prompt.replace_queued` under the same `(admission_id, submission_id)`, which the owner replays if it had committed. Nothing is retried automatically. This is presentation state only; the owner's FIFO never pauses.
- **Health caps.** The new strings live in the small `*_session_commands.ts` catalogs; the large catalogs and `ChatBar` are unchanged.

### Review

One independent review pass (gpt-6-astra) on the earlier head `84abe74a7841` asked for changes: five MAJOR findings, no CRITICAL. The reviewer reproduced findings 1-3 and the hosted-room consumer failure in 5. All five are fixed in this head, each with a failing test first:

1. **A steer could be reported `steered` without reaching an agent.** If the turn had not adopted its agent and construction then failed, the latched text was dropped while the row said `steered`. Steer is now refused before adoption, and an accepted steer is a transfer settled by the receiving claim (see Design notes).
2. **The stream lock was held across the SQLite write,** so a held writer stalled the owner's event loop (~1.6 s measured). No storage wait happens under `event_stream.lock` now; a test holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and checks the loop stays responsive.
3. **A replacement was not bound to the admission it replaced.** Two concurrent replacements of different rows under one `submission_id` both reported success. The binding is now recorded and checked inside the admission transaction; a mismatch is `admission_conflict`.
4. **Desktop dropped the edited text** on a refusal or when the row started mid-edit. It now stays in the composer as an unsent draft with a notice.
5. **Hosted-room rows were offered Steer,** and a steered hosted admission broke its terminal/results reads. Controls are now gated on the session's producer, in both the advertisement and the verbs.

The reviewer confirmed the ordinary replacement transaction cancels the old row and appends at the FIFO tail, older gateways stay Delete-only, canonical rows get no Next, and there is no client-side writer.

### Review round 2

Greptile, kshitijk4poor and teknium1 reviewed `11518d71bb8d`. Every point was checked against the code; the valid ones are fixed in 8 new commits on top, each code fix with a failing test first:
- a steer accepted after the turn's last drain is withdrawn from the agent's buffer and goes back to its queue place instead of settling `steered` (teknium1's live repro);
- a transfer write that may have committed keeps its claim's fence;
- in-flight transfers stay listed as `steering`, so a returned prompt keeps its Desktop card;
- a Save reply settles only its own save and keeps newer text;
- an unconfirmed edit keeps its identity and retries it;
- migrated `desktop` chats get Steer/Edit;
- the new tests wait on events and use bounds of at least 2 s;
- duplicated SQL and checks are shared.

Not changed: an interrupted transfer's completion frame says `cancelled`, as every interrupted turn's does (now documented in the contract). Replacement bindings in `state_meta` are not pruned yet, and a net-zero Edit in a full queue is still refused; both are proposed for #140297.

### Review round 3

A second gpt-6-astra pass on `1a2089d1892d` found two MAJOR and two MINOR issues. Its probes reproduced all four on that head. Each is fixed in a new commit, with a failing test first:
1. Withdrawal matched a transfer's text between newlines in the combined buffer, so a consumed `alpha` was stripped out of a later `alpha\nbeta`: the consumed prompt ran twice and the unread one settled `steered`. Transfers are now settled by ticket (their admission id). The tests cover multiline overlap and identical text on both sides of a drain.
2. A steer that arrived after the last drain went into the finalizer's `pending_steer` follow-up, which the gateway discards while draining for a restart, yet settlement recorded it `steered`. Transfers now stay out of that follow-up and go back to their FIFO place (they run once, or wait queued for the next owner while this one drains). The test uses the real `GatewayRunner._run_agent_drain_pending`.
3. Desktop showed a returned transfer at the bottom of the queue. Cards the owner lists now follow its FIFO order; the regression test has two queued admissions.
4. A `prompt.cancel` that read the row `queued` just before a steer committed reported success while the transfer went on. It is now refused `stale_generation`, the refusal a started row gets.

Also fixed: a stale docstring in a timing test.

### Known limits (reviewer)
- Replacing at the admission queue cap refuses `queue_full`: the cap is counted before the old row retires, and the transaction preserves the original row. (A returned transfer may sit above the cap: it is already-admitted work, and refusing it would lose it.)
- Editing a row with `@terminal:` chips sends the frozen transport text, so the chip display form is not kept on the new admission.
- If the claim's settlement and its unknown-recovery stamp both fail (ownership moved away), a transfer stays `steering`, read as `started`, until the next owner start settles it `interrupted`.
- `gateway.queued_replacement.v1.*` bindings in `state_meta` are not removed by session delete or tombstone prune.
- Queued-row Steer/Edit is Desktop-only; the TUI and the classic CLI keep their current queue controls.
- An adopted agent without `withdraw_steer` (anything other than the in-process `AIAgent`) keeps the old behaviour: an accepted steer counts as consumed.
- A ticketed transfer that no drain consumed stays in the agent's buffer from the end of the turn until the claim's settlement withdraws it. If the same claim runs a follow-up turn first, that turn's drain consumes it and it settles `steered`.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_prompt_queued_controls.py tests/gateway/test_prompt_queued_transfer.py`: 27 passed (3 consecutive runs). The transfer file also covers the first reviewer's repros for findings 1, 2, 3 and 5. From round 2: the late steer (`test_a_steer_settles_steered_only_when_a_drain_of_the_turn_took_it`), a committed-but-failed transfer write, and the `steering` listing. From round 3: identity settlement (`test_each_transfer_settles_by_its_own_identity_whatever_text_another_carries`), the restart-drained follow-up (`test_a_late_transfer_is_never_a_follow_up_that_a_restart_can_discard`), and the cancel race (`test_a_cancel_that_read_the_row_queued_before_a_steer_took_it_is_refused`). `tests/agent/test_steer.py` and `tests/agent/test_turn_finalizer_cleanup_guard.py` cover the agent's ticket ledger and the finalizer's leftover drain.
2. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/composer src/store/pending-submissions.test.ts src/store/composer-queue src/i18n`: 104 files, 775 tests passed. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean.
3. Live (pending): Desktop at this commit against a gateway at this commit.
   1. Queue two prompts during a long turn. Canonical rows show Edit, Steer and Delete, and no Next.
   2. Steer the 2nd: it joins the live turn, never runs on its own, and its receipt ends `steered`.
   3. Steer in the first moment of a turn (before its agent exists): expect a refusal toast, and the row stays queued.
   4. Edit the 1st and save: it moves to the back with the new text.
   5. Edit a row and let the owner start it before saving: the edited text stays in the composer, with a notice.
   6. Steer a row right as the running turn finishes its last reply: either it joins that turn and settles `steered`, or its card comes back in its queue place and it runs once on its own.
   7. Save an edit, keep typing before the answer arrives: the newer text stays.
   8. An older gateway shows Delete only. A hosted-room session shows no Steer/Edit.

selected_prs.title: fix(cli): classic CLI /queue goes into the gateway's durable FIFO (#134889 N5)
selected_prs.body:
Classic CLI `/queue` uses the gateway's durable FIFO.

- N5: when a turn is running, `/queue <prompt>` now goes to the gateway as an ordinary queued admission (`prompt.submit {queued: true}`), the same way Ink and Desktop queue input. It survives an owner restart and runs once, in FIFO order. `/queue list`, `edit`, `rm` and `clear` read and change the owner's queue, and the dock shows it. Refs #134889 (N5)

Design choices
- The CLI keeps no copy it could send again. It only records which admissions it queued, so when the owner starts one, the CLI paints it as a typed turn and streams that admission instead of submitting it a second time.
- One queue: on the gateway's session, a text-only queue-mode Enter (and the steer fallback to queue) is the same FIFO admission as `/queue`, so items keep their entry order and survive a restart. Image follow-ups and non-gateway runs keep the local `_pending_input`.
- A slash command (or typed turn) the input loop takes while this viewer's own `/queue` admission is next in the owner's queue is held until that admission's turn was taken or it left the queue, so `/queue X` then `/new` runs X first. A turn the owner runs meanwhile goes first. The hold is bounded: an `unknown` row (a paused FIFO) never starts one, an idle list beyond the one a settling turn publishes ends it, and it never lasts longer than 2 s.
- `/queue list|rm|edit|clear` act on the session's shared queue: every row the owner publishes for the session, including another window's prompts and automation rows. This is intended (it is the session's queue, as in Ink/Desktop). Docs say so.
- `edit` uses `prompt.replace_queued`, so the edited prompt goes to the back of the queue. `rm` and `clear` use `prompt.cancel`. `move` can't reorder a row the owner holds, so it refuses with a message that says why. The owner's FIFO has no reorder verb. Docs say so.
- A submit whose answer is lost twice (`QueueOutcomeUnknown`) records no admission id: if the owner did queue it, it runs once and shows in `/queue list`, but this CLI doesn't paint its turn live. Noted in the code.
- `/queue` on an idle session is unchanged: the next turn sends it right away.
- If the gateway refuses a queued prompt, the CLI prints the refusal and keeps nothing locally.
- No contract change: `queued` is already part of `prompt.submit`.

Still needs live retest
- Real classic CLI against a live gateway: `/queue X` during a long turn, then `hermes gateway restart`. X should run exactly once and show in the reconnected CLI.
- Queue-mode Enter (`display.busy_input_mode: queue`) typed during a long turn, then `/queue X`: the typed item runs first, then X; `/queue list` shows that order.
- `/queue X` then `/new` (and `/undo`) typed during a long turn: X's turn runs and paints in the old session first, then `/new` runs.
- Typing stays responsive with a paused owner queue (an `unknown` row at the head).
- Queued items after the N2 disconnect.
- The dock shows the owner's queued rows while a turn runs.

selected_prs.title: Kanban workers: delegate_task works again through owner-reserved children (#141793)
selected_prs.body:
`delegate_task` works again inside Kanban cards (and other gateway-managed worker turns). The worker still never creates a child itself: the gateway owner reserves every child execution, and that execution retires with its parent.

> **Stacked on #141906.** This branch sits on #141906's head (`39ee045`), so until that PR lands the diff below includes its 7 commits. Only the last two commits belong to this PR. I'll rebase onto `main` once #141906 merges. The second commit removes #141906's managed-worker "delegation is impossible" diagnostic. That keeps the diagnostic from shipping alongside working delegation.

## Why it broke, and why the block stays
Since #106742 every Kanban card runs in a managed worker. ef52a09a558 (review r4224751560 / r4230769955) removed the `delegation` toolset there on purpose: a delegated child has to hold its own owner-registered execution, and nothing on the owner side could reserve one. That rule is kept. This PR adds the missing owner-side pieces, then drops `WORKER_DISABLED_TOOLSETS`, since the reservation is now the only way a worker can get a child.

## Change
| Piece | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Owner-side child reservation | `gateway/session_worker_child.py` (`child.reserve` on `worker.persist`) | A worker asks on its **own** fenced receipt stream (epoch, assignment, generation, sequence). The owner first verifies the parent's claim. It then mints the child's session row (source `subagent`, the parent as `parent_session_id`, the parent's profile, a `_delegate_from` marker) and a `kind='child'` execution. That execution is bound to the parent's verified pid/birth, a fresh secret from the worker and the connection principal. Caps come from the root session's **frozen** policy (`delegation.max_concurrent_children`, `max_spawn_depth`). A cap hit or a draining owner comes back as a receipt, not an error, so the parent's journal never gets stuck. |
| Child store | `agent/runtime_session_child.py` | The child persists through the ordinary `worker.persist` path under its own claim and can write only its own row. It never binds the process's async-delegation ledger, and closing it ends its execution. `_open_child_session_db` still refuses any route except this reservation, so a worker still never opens SQLite. |
| Restart and adoption | `hermes_state_runtime_workers.py`, `recover_session_inputs` | Every terminal transition of an execution (finish, loss, settlement) retires its live children and ends their rows. An owner restart retires children from the old epoch, which are never adoptable. Only the root execution is recovered as `unknown`, and nothing is replayed. |
| Diagnostic | `tools/tool_search_validation.py`, `agent/conversation_loop.py` (own commit) | Removes #141906's `'delegation'` managed-worker message. A turn with delegation switched off now gets the generic "not available in this execution context". A turn that has `delegate_task` keeps "call it directly". |

## Invariants and tests
| Invariant | Test | Red on base |
|---|---|---|
| The owner admits every child; the worker can't create one; caps hold; the child writes only its own row; the parent's finish retires its children | `tests/hermes_state/test_runtime_worker_children.py::test_owner_mints_caps_and_scopes_children_and_retires_them_with_the_parent` | yes (base compaction: the late child write `DID NOT RAISE`) |
| An owner restart retires in-flight children and never recovers or adopts them | `…::test_owner_restart_mid_child_retires_the_child_and_never_replays_it` | yes (base: the child is left `unknown`) |
| Real daemon + real managed worker + loopback model: the child completes and its result gets back to the parent | `tests/gateway/test_managed_worker_delegation.py` (2 tests: completion; kill-and-restart mid-child) | yes (base: `delegate_task` is never offered) |
| The diagnostic doesn't contradict working delegation | `tests/tools/test_managed_worker_tool_diagnostics.py` (rewritten) | n/a (replaces #141906's pin) |

Profile scope: the reservation rides the parent's authenticated connection (`_claim` refuses `profile_mismatch`), and the child row gets the parent's `profile_name`. Usage is booked on the child's own row (`input_tokens=7` in the live run). Deleting the parent cascades to the child row and retires its ledger rows.

## Live evidence: real `hermes gateway run --force`, real Kanban dispatcher, real managed worker, loopback model
Run in a scratch `HERMES_HOME`; `hermes_cli.__file__` was printed for each leg.
- **base (origin/main):** card `done`, summary `child said: NOTHING`. `delegate_task` was never offered and no child session exists.
- **head:** card `done`, summary `child said: CHILD_ANSWER_42`. Model trace: `delegate_task → CHILD_ANSWER_42 → kanban_complete`. Child execution ended `terminal`; subagent row `agent_close`, `input_tokens=7`.
- **head, owner killed mid-child:** before the kill the child was `running`. After `kill` and a fresh `gateway run --force` it was `terminal`, its row `agent_close`, and the lost turn was not replayed.

Tests: 104 passed across the touched suites and their neighbours (delegate, worker receipts/adoption, managed worker execution, #141906's suites). `scripts/check --only health` is clean.

Fixes #141793
Part of #134889

![kanban-delegation](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf1d68/6_i-XggT73qTpnk4dReiP_soteBHRk.png)

## Review follow-up

Restacked onto the current #141906 head `9dc13ca` (the diagnostics conflict is resolved by keeping #141906's session-unavailability path and dropping only the managed-worker "use kanban_create" alternative, which this PR makes untrue). New commit `bf996b0`:

| Finding | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1: with Relay on, the child is still built on Relay's loop, so `synchronous_rpc_on_event_loop` | **Fixed**: every RPC from the child store hops off a running loop (the reservation, the constructor's `bind_session_state` reads, run, and the close's `execution.finish`), with contextvars copied | New real-daemon test `test_relay_driven_worker_builds_and_runs_its_child_off_the_relay_loop` (native NeMo Relay file sink): red on `ada8bd4`'s code (`status=error, synchronous_rpc_on_event_loop`), green here. The reviewer's nested/batch/cancel/Relay matrix (4 tests) also passes |
| P2: an early close finishes the child but leaves its session row open | **Fixed**: a child's own `execution.finish` ends its row (`agent_close`) | `test_a_child_store_closed_before_any_turn_...` goes red when close skips finish; `test_depth_cap_...` goes red without the end |
| 6 untested invariants (S4 depth, S5 profile, S6 parent verify, S7 draining, S9 sibling cleanup, S10 close→finish) | **Covered**: each sabotage now turns a test red except S5 | S5 (child `profile_name=None`) is masked by design: `insert_session_row_in_transaction` stamps the store's own profile onto a NULL, so the child still gets the parent's profile. The test asserts that outcome |
| P2: reserved row loses its constructor settings | **Fixed**: `session.create` merges the constructor keys beside `_delegate_from` | red on base (`{'_delegate_from'}` only) |

selected_prs.title: fix(gateway): the dock keeps background subagents across a parent rebuild
selected_prs.body:
In the CLI (and any client of the canonical gateway's `subagent.list`), background subagents disappear from the live-work dock after the session's cached agent is rebuilt, while the status bar keeps counting them (`⛓ 2` with only a `Processes` block in the dock).

## Repro (real `hermes chat` on `origin/main`)

1. Start a background process and a `background=true` delegation → dock shows `Subagents · 1 live` and `Processes · 1 running`.
2. `/reasoning high` (or `/model`, a policy refresh, idle eviction — anything that evicts the cached agent), then any turn.
3. Dock: the Subagents block is gone; status bar still shows `⛓ 1`.

## Cause

`gateway/session_ancillary.py::subagent_records` matched a child only by object ancestry to the **resident** parent agent (plus the fallback-eviction case from #139884). After a rebuild the child's `_delegate_parent_ref` points at the old parent object, so the read-only roster returned nothing. `delegate_task(action="list")` and the TUI's `subagent.list` already follow the conversation by durable owner id; this path did not.

## Fix

The read-only roster also accepts a child whose `owner_agent_session_id` is in this session's compression lineage **and** whose session DB is the same file (so another profile's child never matches). Control (`subagent.steer` / `subagent.interrupt`) and `subagent.tail` stay pinned to the resident parent; `include_fallback_evicted=False` callers are unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Live: background process + delegation, `/reasoning high`, a turn | before: Subagents block gone, `⛓ 1`. After: `Subagents · 1 live` + `Processes · 1 running` both still docked |
| New `test_subagent_roster_survives_a_parent_rebuild` (child kept for the rebuilt parent; another profile's DB and another conversation excluded; control path still empty) | passes; fails on `origin/main` (`[] == ['live-child']`) |
| Existing fallback-roster test (stale child with no session DB stays hidden) | passes |
| 10 test files touching `subagent.list` / `session_ancillary` / the dock | 64 passed |
| ruff, `scripts/check --only health` | clean |

selected_prs.title: Kanban: a timed-out managed run is recorded timed_out, not crashed
selected_prs.body:
When a managed Kanban run hits `max_runtime_seconds`, it is now recorded as `timed_out` again. Before this fix the crash sweep picked it up on the next tick and recorded it as `crashed`. This was the red `test_real_dispatcher_lifecycle[timeout]` on main's push run (39425878247) and on unrelated PRs such as #141928.

**Root cause:** the under-lock `owner_reclaim_blocked` re-check added in bdbee23c1e9 runs after the SIGTERM wait, and by then it sees a pause the timeout itself caused. Killing the spawned worker takes the bound interpreter down too (`_watch_submitter`). The owner then settles the admission as `unknown`, so `owner_reclaim_paused` becomes true, and because the run has a `worker_bound` event, `owner_attempt_provably_over` refuses to rule on it. `enforce_max_runtime` then skipped the release and returned `[]`, and the next crash sweep recorded the run as `crashed`. The outcome depended on whether the owner settled the admission inside the 0.5 s poll window.

## Changes
- `kanban_owner_recovery.owner_reclaim_blocked_after_kill` is the under-lock re-check for paths that have just signalled the worker. It is `owner_reclaim_blocked(..., crash_sweep=True)`: a dead bound interpreter is the one this path just stopped, so it no longer blocks the release.
- `enforce_max_runtime`, `detect_stale_running` and `release_stale_claims` use it for the re-check inside the transaction. The first look before the kill is unchanged. `reconcile_orphaned_running` never sends a signal, so it keeps the plain gate.
- The invariant from bdbee23c1e9 still holds: if an interpreter that bound after the first look is still **live**, it keeps its claim. `test_an_interpreter_bound_after_the_gate_keeps_its_claim[ttl|stale|runtime]` stays green unchanged.
- New regression test `test_a_timed_out_managed_run_is_booked_timed_out_not_left_for_the_crash_sweep` uses a real worker and a real bound-interpreter process. The signal hook kills the interpreter and sets the admission to `unknown`, the way the owner does.

## Validation
| Check | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| New regression test | **FAIL** (`assert [] == ['t_slow']`) | pass |
| `test_session_kanban.py`, `flake_hammer.py` (2×nproc CPU spinners, 6 runs) | **2/6 failed**, CI's exact receipt (`timed_out: []`, `run_outcome: 'crashed'`) | **0/6 failed** |
| `test_session_kanban.py`, unloaded, `HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0` | 1/1 failed | 3/3 passed |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban*.py` + `tests/gateway/test_kanban_recovery.py` | — | 540 passed, 0 failed |
| `scripts/check --only health,ruff,no-tmp,footguns` | — | ok |

The `BrokenPipeError` in the CI log is a side effect, not the cause: the probe's loopback model writes its reply to an interpreter the timeout has already killed.

selected_prs.title: Desktop's stale-gateway restart no longer leaves the gateway as an app child that gets killed and blocks quit
selected_prs.body:
When Desktop restarts a gateway that runs older code on a machine with no installed gateway service, the replacement gateway now starts on its own in the background. It no longer becomes a child of the app that gets killed after 120 s and holds app quit open.

## Changes

- **`hermes gateway restart --detach`** (new flag, `hermes_cli/subcommands/gateway.py`): with no installed service, the manual fallback starts the replacement the same way `hermes gateway ensure` starts a missing owner (`spawn_unmanaged_gateway`) and then returns. It no longer runs `run_gateway()` in the calling process. The new code is `gateway_supervised_restart.start_restart_replacement` → `gateway_runtime_start.start_detached_replacement`; the `gateway.py` facade does not grow.
- **`--force` and `--all`:** `restart --force --detach` passes `--force` on to the background replacement, so a named profile under a multiplexer is not stopped and then refused. `restart --all --detach` starts the host gateway through the existing detached `--replace` launcher instead of running `run_gateway` in the caller. That launcher now pins `--profile default` for the root home, so the unsupervised child no longer follows the sticky `active_profile`. This also fixes the named-profile `--all` path, the macOS launchctl fallback and the migration spawn, which share the command.
- **Desktop** (`restartLocalGatewayOwner` → `runGatewayOwnerRestart` in `apps/desktop/electron/local-gateway.ts`): passes `--detach`. This covers the stale-owner restart at startup and the Models-page "Restart Hermes" button, which uses the same function. A runtime older than the flag rejects it with an argparse "unrecognized arguments: --detach" error (exit 2). Only in that case Desktop retries once without the flag, so older service-backed installs keep their working restart.
- **Updater recovery restart** (`hermes_cli/update_restart_recovery.py`): passes `--detach`. This bounded call has a 90 s captured timeout, so it had the same problem: it became a service-less profile's gateway and was then killed.
- **Unchanged:** restarts through a service (systemd/launchd), an external supervisor or a Windows task, and a person running `hermes gateway restart` in a terminal (it still runs in the foreground there).
- **Docs:** a `--detach` row in `website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md`.

**Root cause:** with no service installed, `_cmd_restart` stops the old owner and then calls `run_gateway()` in the foreground, so Desktop's bounded, piped `hermes gateway restart` client turned into the new long-lived gateway.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_restart_no_unit_linger.py::test_detached_restart_without_service_never_runs_the_gateway_in_the_caller` | **red** on `origin/main` `gateway.py` (the caller runs the gateway), **green** on this branch |
| `test_detached_restart_keeps_force_for_the_replacement`, `test_detached_restart_all_never_runs_the_host_gateway_in_the_caller` (the latter with a sticky `active_profile=work`) | **red** on the previous head, **green** on b7126b43e8e |
| `electron/local-gateway-restart-detach.test.ts` (real bounded client, fake `hermes`) | the older-runtime case fails without the fallback and passes with it; the current-runtime case asserts `--detach` is sent |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_host_verbs.py::test_named_profile_restart_all_reaches_the_all_aware_branch` | only its `_restart_all` stub signature changed (it now accepts `detach`); the assertion is unchanged |
| `test_gateway_host_verbs.py::test_named_profile_restart_all_with_host_down_restarts_the_default_root` | `"--profile" not in cmd` (meaning "not the named profile") becomes "the selector is `default` and `leinad` is not in argv" |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_restart_recovery.py`: two argv assertions | now also expect `--detach`. The `--interrupt` invariant they pin (the update owns this restart, so a live session must not strand the profile on pre-update code) is unchanged |
| restart test files via `scripts/run_tests.sh`; desktop vitest; `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json` | pass |
| `python3 scripts/check` | 12 checks ok; health 0 blocking; `gateway.py` does not grow |
| ruff | clean |
| install-e2e run 39531779285 (before the fix) | Linux legs `installer-script+desktop -> installer-script (HEAD -> NEXT)` and similar were cancelled at the 60-min job timeout after `Desktop did not close gracefully`. The Desktop log shows `owner runs <HEAD> ... restarting it` but never `[gateway] hermes --profile default gateway restart exited`: the restart client never exited because it had become the gateway |
| Live CI proof | will come from the release proof run (install-e2e Linux HEAD -> NEXT legs) dispatched after this PR |

Two tests in `test_gateway_host_verbs.py` / `test_gateway_multiplex_lifecycle.py` fail locally the same way on `origin/main` code. The cause is `tests/home_io_guard.py` running inside a worktree, which is environmental and unrelated to this change.

selected_prs.title: feat: install OpenCode 2 into a private npm prefix
selected_prs.body:
Code changes: +519 -69  
Tests: +679 -28  
Others: +3 -0  

## Summary

- First-use OpenCode 2 migration gets a separate 30-minute readiness budget and continues when a request stops waiting; daemon shutdown still cancels it. The three-second auth-command timeout starts after migration finishes.
- OpenCode 2 npm installs use a daemon-configured private prefix, validate that private destination instead of npm's global prefix, and report the private binary directory.
- OpenCode 2 data-home resolution rejects relative paths and fails closed; the first v2 operation migrates any legacy shared store into the isolated home without overwriting existing isolated state. SQLite is copied through a consistent snapshot, while migration locking, file copies, and snapshot retries honor caller cancellation.
- OpenCode binary discovery and version probing share one overall deadline. Classified major-version mismatches remain actionable only after a complete search; incomplete searches preserve timeout or cancellation errors.
- Settings keeps installation controls available for a wrong-major binary while showing the actionable mismatch reason in the row and tooltip.
- The system-install service no longer imports the OpenCode adapter; install path policy is supplied by daemon composition through service dependencies.

## Tests

- All 23 GitHub checks passed on `d84221bc30be83610f4125542a781de7058a4342`. Local workflow runners could not start because Docker Desktop rejected the Docker socket bind mount; the frontend runner was stopped while startup was stalled. Native Windows checks were verified in GitHub CI.
- The migration-budget fix adds regressions for migration exceeding the auth-command timeout, readiness work exceeding the ordinary 10-second auth budget, canceled waiters, daemon shutdown, and explicit auth-timeout overrides. Complete OpenCode 2 and agent-service race suites and native CLI E2E pass in an isolated environment; the full native backend run encountered host/tool-dependent failures.
- Added regression coverage for read-only global npm prefixes, private-prefix reporting, legacy data migration, live WAL snapshots, rollback-journal exclusion, migration cancellation, relative data-home rejection, shared probe deadlines, mismatch error priority, and the visible Settings diagnostic.
- Focused OpenCode tests, race tests, affected-package compilation, and `go vet` pass locally. The full backend suite also ran offline; unrelated host-dependent tests remain environment-sensitive.

## Risks

- Migration remains capped at 30 minutes. A store that cannot finish within that budget reports an authentication-check timeout and retries; explicit readiness timeout overrides are preserved.
- Legacy OpenCode state is copied on first OpenCode 2 use and retained in the original shared store for OpenCode 1; subsequent state diverges between the two isolated homes.
- A real Windows npm OpenCode shim and a real npm install remain covered by CI/fakes rather than a local end-to-end install.

selected_prs.title: fix(chat): keep ACP prompt receipts acknowledgeable after a host rejection
selected_prs.body:
Fixes #6222

## Summary

When a Chat prompt reached the persistent ACP host before AO had acknowledged the previous turn's terminal result, the host refused it locally with `previous ACP prompt is active or not acknowledged`. That refusal has no event ID. `finishPrompt` then set `terminalEventID` to the empty ID, which erased the outstanding receipt. When the controller later committed the original result and sent its ACK, `AcknowledgeProviderEvent` saw a mismatch and returned nil without notifying the host. The host kept its pending result and refused every later prompt with the same `-32602` error until the session was restarted or switched to TUI and back. Both reports on the issue match this: the OMP incident, and the Claude Code session that recovered only after a TUI round trip.

The fix: only a durable host receipt (a non-empty event ID) replaces the outstanding `terminalEventID`. A host-local rejection still settles its own turn as failed, but the original receipt stays acknowledgeable. Once that ACK goes out, the host accepts prompts again.

Hosts that are already wedged recover without extra repair work. After the update restarts the daemon, `ActivateLiveReconnect` acknowledges a committed pending result.

## Not in this PR

The issue also asks to serialize the `SteerOrSend` no-active-turn fallback with terminal projection. That moved to #6360. Routing the fallback through the busy queue conflicts with the #4861 failed-turn queue hold, so for now the behavior stays as it is. With this fix, losing that race costs one failed replacement turn instead of wedging the session.

## Tests

- New test `TestPersistentACPLateAckSurvivesHostLocalPromptRejection` uses the real persistent host and a fake ACP provider, with completed and failed originals. It runs the original turn without an ACK, then a replacement turn that the host rejects with no event ID, then a late ACK of the original. The next prompt must reach the provider and complete, and the provider must see exactly 2 prompts. Without the fix both subtests fail: the turn after the late ACK is still refused.
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/` passes.
- I did not run golangci-lint locally because it isn't installed here. `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

## Risks

Low. The only behavior change: a completion without an event ID no longer clears the stored receipt. Persistent host responses always carry an event ID, and non-persistent processes never set one, so for them the field stays empty as before.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

selected_prs.title: fix(chat): keep orchestrator history and queued prompts on the project conversation
selected_prs.body:
Code changes: +340 -25\
Tests: +493 -1\
Others: +236 -1 (generated sqlc)

## What

The project orchestrator's Chat now shows its real history, and prompts typed while it was provisioning drain in the conversation its controller uses. Before this change, the orchestrator's chat could show a blank history with a message stuck under "Queued", while the session showed Idle.

## Why

Fixes #6523.

A message sent to an orchestrator while it provisions is queued by `ensureConversation` in a **session-scoped** conversation, because no controller exists yet. When the controller starts, `Start` opens the **project-scoped** conversation, which is where orchestrators keep their narrative. Both rows then have `current_session_id` set to the orchestrator.

`SelectConversationBySession` was `WHERE current_session_id = ? LIMIT 1` with no ordering. On the `current_session_id` index it returns the older row, which is the provisioning one. Every session-keyed read (the snapshot, steer, the queue editor, the handoff lookup) therefore saw a conversation holding only the stranded prompt. Meanwhile the controller drained and wrote to the project row.

## How

1. **One write at first start.** When an orchestrator's **first** controller opens the project conversation, `Start` calls `CreateProjectConversationAdoptingQueue`. In one transaction under `writeMu`, it:
   - rebinds (or creates) the project conversation;
   - records the context-reset boundary;
   - **moves** the provisioning row's turns, messages, activities, and queued-edit receipts into it;
   - detaches the provisioning row.

   The rebind and the move share that transaction, so a prompt sent meanwhile lands either in the provisioning row, and moves with the rest, or in the project row after them. Queue order and the timeline agree.
2. **Rows keep their IDs.** Turns keep their ID and `requested_at`, so a turn ID the queue editor already holds still resolves for edit and cancel, and queued-edit receipts keep a retried edit idempotent. Messages and activities are offset past the project row's latest sequence, which puts them after the boundary just recorded. Excerpt references in queued delivery content are retargeted from the provisioning conversation to the project conversation, because drain checks each reference against the conversation it runs in.
3. **Nothing is left where no lookup can find it.** Every turn in the provisioning row moves, whatever its state, including one an interrupted drain left reserved (`promotion_started_at` set) and one with no user message. The only exception is a turn whose prompt already reached the project row under the same `client_message_id`, since moving it would break that row's unique client id. That turn is cancelled before the row is detached. A retried start finds nothing to move.
4. **A queued append checks its row is still bound.** `AppendUserMessage` for a pre-controller turn now checks, inside the same write, that the conversation's `current_session_id` is still the session. A Send that read the provisioning row before the move gets `ErrConversationRebound`, looks the session's conversation up again, and queues in the project row.
5. **Migration 0197** detaches the stale session-scoped row on databases older builds left bound to both rows. That fixes every other `current_session_id` consumer at once: the 0190 hibernation CDC trigger's unordered lookup, the branch-root triggers (0087, 0101, 0149), `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider`, and `ResetConversationAgentOverridesForSession`. A session still waiting for its first controller is left alone, because its start moves the queue itself. The stale prompts on already-split rows are not replayed: once that orchestrator has run, replaying an old opening prompt would repeat work.
6. **Lookup safety net.** `SelectConversationBySession` still orders `scope = 'project'` first, with a deterministic tiebreak.

Only a session that is still provisioning, has never had a controller, and has no provider history counts as the first controller. `Start` reads the session once and shares that one check between the move and `queuedBeforeFirstController`.

**Why not bind the project conversation during provisioning?** That's the smaller change: create the project-scoped row in `ensureConversation`. But it files the queued prompt *before* the context-reset boundary that `Start` records for a fresh orchestrator, and `LoadConversationSnapshotPage` hides everything at or before that boundary. The prompt would drain but never show in the timeline. `TestOrchestratorOpeningPromptDrainsInProjectConversation` fails that way, for both a new project and a replacement orchestrator, when the scope is changed in `ensureConversation` instead. Binding early would also expose the queue for the whole provisioning window to the controller of an orchestrator being replaced, which can still be running on that conversation (see follow-up).

**Intentional omission:** no unique index on `conversations.current_session_id`. That would be a schema change with its own rollout.

**Follow-up, not in this PR:** `RetireForReplacement` does not stop a Chat orchestrator's controller. `terminateNativeSession` only handles TUI sessions, unlike `Kill`, which calls `stopChatBestEffort`. I confirmed this by reading the code, not live. It is outside this fix.

## Testing

Regression tests, on the real SQLite store with the fake provider:

- `TestOrchestratorOpeningPromptDrainsInProjectConversation` (`new_project`, `replacement`): the prompt queued during provisioning drains in the project conversation and is visible in the paged timeline.
- `TestQueuedSendRacingFirstStartLandsInProjectConversation`: a Send that read the provisioning row before the move queues in the project row, after the moved prompt, in both the queue and the timeline.
- `TestStrandedPromptFromEarlierRunIsNotReplayed`: an orchestrator that is already split shows its project transcript, and the stale prompt is not replayed.
- `TestFirstOrchestratorControllerMovesProvisioningQueue`: the move keeps turn IDs and order, places the prompts after the boundary, retargets excerpt references, keeps a queued-edit retry idempotent, moves a turn an interrupted drain reserved, settles a turn already delivered under its client id, detaches the row, and is a no-op on retry.
- `TestQueuedAppendRefusesConversationTheSessionNoLongerHolds`: an append to the moved-out row returns `ErrConversationRebound`.
- `TestConversationForSessionPrefersProjectNarrativeOverProvisioningRow`: the session lookup returns the project row.
- `TestMigration0197DetachesSplitOrchestratorConversations`: the migration detaches the stale row, keeps a still-provisioning session's queue, and leaves unrelated rows bound.

Red/green: on unmodified `main`, the service tests and the lookup test fail with the reported symptoms. The orchestrator reads the session row, the replacement's prompt never drains, and the split session shows the provisioning row. All pass with this change.

The seventh, `opencodev2`'s `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects/malformed_version`, picks up the OpenCode 1.18.31 binary installed at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` on this machine. Code changes: +1587 -41

Others: +630 -25  

## What

Usage limits appear as a compact, neutral notice with a warning icon, local reset time, and countdown. Before reset, offer **Auto-resume at reset**. Once selected, keep **Cancel auto-resume** available while consent remains armed, including after the deadline during wake or transient backoff; show a localized waiting-to-retry state then. Show **Resume** when ready and unarmed, and remove the composer notice when a retry starts.

## Why

Quota refusals currently look like generic agent failures, and Retry gives no indication of when the prompt can run again. Users need a visible recovery action and an option to continue automatically after reset.

## How

- Expose a durable human-prompt fact on full and paged snapshots. Composer Resume/Cancel and earlier quota-failure Resume use it when the original prompt is outside the loaded history page; ordinary Retry and rollback retain their existing behavior.
- Recognize known quota refusals and anchor clock-only reset times to the original failure in the provider timezone. Nonexistent or repeated DST wall clocks remain manual; explicit UTC timestamps and trusted stored absolute deadlines are preserved.
- Normalize native Codex `usageLimitExceeded` refusals, preserve trustworthy in-turn UTC account reset metadata, and retain standalone quota errors on failed completions that omit the final error. Ambiguous metadata and display-only dates remain manual.
- Recognize Claude individual-spend/no-quota refusals and verify its native ACP terminal-failure extension through the real AO driver and persistent host.
- Translate recovery messages, controls, and countdown units for all eight supported locales.
- Persist opt-in consent and the absolute deadline on the failed turn; the daemon resumes it even after the view closes, the provider hibernates, or AO restarts.
- Reuse durable retry idempotency and recheck current lineage, delivery confirmation, and later work before dispatch.
- Consume still-armed, due consent in the retry-insert transaction, checking account history at that same boundary. Cancellation and account changes that commit before insertion prevent dispatch; manual retry remains idempotent.
- Skip per-turn validation until its stored reset time. Preserve consent through transient errors with 30-second backoff; up to four independent attempts can progress while other providers wake. The coordinator mutex guards bookkeeping only, and shutdown joins scheduled work before teardown. A 90-second attempt budget accommodates the existing 60-second wake.
- Keep earlier limited prompts manually recoverable after reset, preserving retry errors and avoiding duplicate controls for the composer-managed source.
- Auto-resume applies to a confirmed failed human turn with a known reset time; unknown reset times remain manual.
- Reuse the merged account service for a fresh, targeted quota read at the deadline. Shared native reset validation can postpone an existing deadline; a two-second best-effort probe never creates consent or replaces a trusted turn reset with an ambiguous display value.
- Commit account bindings and cancellation of armed consent together. Source-time binding history and retry receipts prevent scheduling an old-account or already-retried prompt.
- Use generated timestamp migrations `20261019220421171_usage_limit_auto_resume.sql` and `20261019220421514_usage_limit_reset_cdc.sql`, leaving main’s shipped `0213`/`0214` intact. Relocate only identified quota-preview receipts, preserving receipt IDs, saved prompts, deadlines, and consent; foreign `0201` history is retained.

selected_prs.title: fix(kanban): show Interrupted on a card after the agent is stopped
selected_prs.body:
## Problem

When you stop a chat agent, its card on the board keeps saying "Awaiting PR". Stopping the agent only makes the session idle, and the board treats an idle session with no PR as finished work waiting for a PR. The chat already knows the turn was interrupted, but the board never read that.

## Fix

The board now reads how the session's latest chat turn ended. If it was interrupted and the agent is idle, the card says **Interrupted** and stays in its current column, usually Building. A session with only artifact output stays in Validating.

- Sending a new message clears it, and the card goes back to "Working".
- A queued message you withdrew does not clear it.
- If the agent exited, the card says "Exited" as before.
- Cards with a PR still show their PR status (CI, review), because that tells you more.

The interrupted check is one database query per board load, covering every session at once. A single-session read runs the same query for that one session. The query uses the existing indexes on conversations and turns.

## Changes

- `backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go`: new `Interrupted` session fact and new `Interrupted` display status, used in the Building and artifact states.
- `queries/conversations.sql` + `conversation_store.go`: `ListInterruptedSessions` picks each session's conversation the same way `SelectConversationBySession` does. It ignores cancelled, rolled-back and promoted turns.
- `service/session`: the session list and single-session reads pass the fact to the board.
- API spec and `schema.ts` regenerated. The frontend label is added in all 8 languages. Mobile shows the daemon's `displayStatus` text as-is, so it needs no change.

## Not covered

Terminal (TUI) sessions. When you press Esc in one, the agent's hooks may not report anything, so the card could keep saying "Working". That is a separate problem in how terminal sessions report activity.

## Testing

- `go test ./pkg/contract/ ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/httpd/...` pass.
- New tests: how the status is chosen (idle, active, exited, artifact output); the store query (interrupt, withdrawn queued prompt, new turn); the service list and single-session reads.
- Frontend: the translation files and `SessionsBoard` tests pass.
- To test by hand: start a chat session with no PR, stop it mid-turn, and check the card says Interrupted. Send a message and check it goes back to Working.

selected_prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep a revived subagent on the account that holds its prompt cache
selected_prs.body:
## What

My parked subagents kept coming back on a different Claude account than the one they'd been using, which threw away their whole prompt cache, so now a revived subagent stays on the account its own transcript was pinned to.

With several OAuth accounts for one provider, a subagent is pinned to an account and its prompt cache lives there. Reviving a parked subagent re-runs `createAgentSession` with its original spawn options, including `credentialSourceSessionId`. That copied the parent's account affinity onto the child first. `seedCredentialPins` then refused to restore the child's own transcript pin, because a live affinity for another account already existed. The child's next request went to the parent's account and re-wrote its whole cached prefix there.

`SessionsApi.inherit` now takes an optional filter, called with each provider and whether the source affinity is an explicit user pin. `createAgentSession` passes `(provider, explicit) => explicit || !ownPins.has(provider)`: the parent's automatic affinity yields to a provider the child's transcript already pins, and an explicit `/session pin` in the parent still reaches the child with its explicit flag, so reserve ranking cannot evict it (#11939). A fresh subagent has no pins and inherits everything as before. The child's account pool still applies.

## Why

Two observed revivals, both on Opus with three subscription accounts:

| revival | child's own account | served by | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| reviewer subagent, idle 41 min | account B (warm) | account C | cache read 0, write 189,931 |
| research subagent, idle 15 min | account B (warm) | account A | cache read 0, write 172,836 |

Account policies (reserve, allowance) still evict a revived child's automatic pin as they would any warm automatic pin; this only stops the parent's automatic affinity overriding the child's own.

Non-goals: no change to how the parent's account is chosen, fresh-spawn inheritance, or cold revival from disk (no `credentialSourceSessionId`; the child keeps its own pin, as on `main`).

## Testing

Revival cases in `packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-subagent-auth-inheritance.test.ts`, each through `createAgentSession` with the parent as `credentialSourceSessionId`:

- Parent automatically on A, child transcript on B: child resolves B. Fails when every parent affinity is copied, as on `main`.
- Parent explicitly pinned to A, child on B: child resolves A.
- Parent explicitly pinned to B, child on B, B inside its reserve: child stays on B.
- Parent explicitly pinned to B before the child's first run, child reopened from its session file with a newer transcript pin, B inside its reserve: stays on B.
- Parent explicitly pinned to A, child pool allows only B: child resolves B. Passes with and without this change; it guards pool ordering.

The second, third and fourth fail with the previous filter (`provider => !ownPins.has(provider)`).

```
bun test packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-subagent-auth-inheritance.test.ts
```

Also run: credential-pin, persisted-revive, subagent auth and account-pool dispose tests with the file above (69 pass); `packages/ai` affinity, restriction and selection tests (99 pass); `bun run check:ts` passes. Rust checks not run.

selected_prs.title: fix(coding-agent): read omp usage --history from the auth broker
selected_prs.body:
## What

`omp usage --history` kept telling me nothing was recorded on both of my machines while the broker held thousands of snapshots, so it now asks the broker, the same way `omp usage clients` already does.

On an auth-broker client, `omp usage --history` prints the broker host's usage-limit history (with the same `--days` and `--provider` filters) instead of always reporting "No usage history recorded yet". Without a broker it still reads the local agent DB. The broker-or-local choice now lives in one helper, `resolveBrokerClient`, shared by the `history` and `clients` paths of `runUsageCommand`.

## Why

In a broker deployment the broker host performs every upstream usage fetch and records the snapshots. The client's credential store is the broker's remote store, which deliberately keeps no history (`UsageLedgerStore` documents this), so `authStorage.usage.history()` returns nothing on every client. `omp usage clients` and the stats dashboard already read the broker for exactly this reason; `--history` was the one surface still reading the local store.

Non-goals: filtering history by an `OMP_AUTH_BROKER_ACCOUNT_POOL_FILE` pool (the broker token already sees every account, and `usage clients` does not filter either), and any change to how history rows are rendered.

## Testing

- Live, against a running broker holding 1,835 snapshots from the last 24 h. On a broker client, 18.7.0 `omp usage --history --days 1 --provider openai-codex` prints "No usage history recorded for provider "openai-codex" yet."; this branch prints both Codex accounts' 5 hour and 7 day series, 25 snapshots each. The broker host's own omp (also configured as a broker client) printed the same empty message on 18.7.0.
- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/usage-cli-history.test.ts`: starts a real broker on loopback with recorded snapshots for two providers and asserts `runUsageCommand({ history: true, json: true, provider: "anthropic" })` returns exactly the broker's two anthropic rows. With the fix reverted it receives `[]` and fails.
- `bun test test/usage-cli.test.ts test/usage-cli-extension-usage.test.ts`: 43 pass.
- `bun run check:ts`: every package's `check:types` passes; `check:tools` reports only the 19 files that are already unformatted on `main`.

selected_prs.title: feat(coding-agent): support ACP _session/steering for mid-turn client steering
selected_prs.body:
Human sentence: I needed this to make steering work with agent-shell in emacs, and now it works with this change!

## What

Implements the `_session/steering` ACP extension method — the convention shipped by claude-agent-acp and codex-acp (spec proposal: `session/inject`, agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol#1261) — and advertises it via top-level `_meta.steering.supported` in the `initialize` response:

- **Turn in flight** (streaming, or a `session/prompt` turn reserved but still dispatching) → prompt queued on `AgentSession.steer()` → `{ outcome: "injected", queue: "steering" }`; the steer joins the client's own pending turn instead of queueing a second prompt behind it
- **In flight + `_meta.steering.queue: "followUp"`** (omp-specific opt-in) → `AgentSession.followUp()` → `{ outcome: "injected", queue: "followUp" }`
- **Idle** → always `{ outcome: "promptRequired", queue }`; content stays unconsumed so the host submits it via `session/prompt` and keeps owning the turn. omp deliberately never returns `startedNewTurn` (claude-agent-acp's behavior without the `idleBehavior` opt-in) because a detached turn has no `session/prompt` response to carry a failed start — the client would see neither completion nor error (claude-agent-acp#903)
- Session refusal → `{ outcome: "failed", reason }`; malformed params (including block-level shape) / unknown session → JSON-RPC `-32602` errors

Review findings from @roboomp and the Codex reviews are addressed. The follow-up Codex round (on `267efc2`) showed the bridge-level busy-check + post-hoc withdrawal design was still racy, so admission moved into the engine:

- **`267efc2`** — pending-dispatch busy window classified (`isPromptTurnInFlight` ∥ `isStreaming`, concurrent-request test); detached `startedNewTurn` path removed (idle always answers `promptRequired`, so a failed start can't be invisible); prompt blocks validated before `#convertPromptBlocks` dereferences them (`-32602` on the wire).
- **`dbcf5d3` (follow-ups + user report)** — admission is now `AgentSession.joinActiveTurn()`: one atomic engine primitive that classifies the run and enqueues (`#queueUserMessage` re-checks liveness after its awaits and skips the idle drain for this path). A steer racing `session/cancel` or arriving while no run is live simply classifies as not-admitted (`promptRequired`), with nothing ever stranded on an idle queue — which also removes the withdrawal-identity ambiguity (nothing is withdrawn; duplicate-text matching is moot). Block-type lookup is own-key (`Object.hasOwn`) so inherited names (`constructor`, …) return `-32602`, and an unknown session maps to `-32602` invalid-params instead of a generic `-32603`. Plus the actual gap found in use: **a steer sent while a permission elicit is open now supersedes the dialog** — the gate races the session's steering-arrival signal, the superseded call surfaces as a cancelled permission (a normal tool error), and the message injects at the next batch boundary instead of waiting behind the dialog. Covered by a real-`AgentSession` test driving the exact scenario.
- **`38382bc` (dbcf5d3 review round)** — the admission recheck refuses on `#abortInProgress` (raised synchronously at `abort()` entry, while `isStreaming` can stay true until cleanup), so a cancel racing an image steer's preprocessing can no longer land it on the queue the abort drains; the prompt pre-dispatch window deliberately answers `promptRequired` (nothing to inject into yet — the host's resubmission queues behind the dispatching turn), documented and covered by real-session regressions; superseded permission elicits are now **cancelled on the wire** via a new `$/cancel_request` primitive (`RpcConnection.requestCancellable` → `AgentSideConnection.requestPermissionWithCancel`), with the ACP bridge racing the session's steering-arrival signal so no live `session/request_permission` dialog outlives its tool call; and `_session/steering` rejects null/non-object params as `-32602` before any dereference can surface `-32603`.
- **`9bb4fed` (38382bc review round)** — the post-settle idle drain is gated on ACP turn ownership (a queued steer stays queued and visible instead of auto-continuing unowned; the in-flight end-of-turn continuation is unchanged), the wire elicit's own cancel-rejection maps to the steer-winning outcome with no unhandled rejection on the pre-aborted early exit, and idle slash commands are handed back unconsumed (`promptRequired`) instead of failing.
- The residual end-of-turn window (a steer admitted after the loop's final queue poll parks when the settle drain is blocked) is deliberately not wedged here — the structural fix is engine turn-end protocol work: #16011.

selected_prs.title: feat(acp): support /mcp reauth outside the TUI
selected_prs.body:
Human sentence: I use omp through emacs agent-shell and mcp auth is core to me having omp interact with cloud services, so having this work is a huge relief. I'd love to get this into main so I don't have to run off my own local build :)

## What

`/mcp reauth <name>` used to answer "OAuth or browser flows only available in the TUI client" whenever it arrived over ACP or text mode. As I put it when I hit this: there's no obviously good reason why omp couldn't open the browser when invoked via acp — omp runs on the user's machine either way, so the browser can open exactly as in the TUI.

Rather than fork the TUI's flow, this extracts the UI-agnostic reauth engine into `src/mcp/oauth-reauth.ts` and drives it from both surfaces: server lookup (user over project, standalone `mcp.json`/`.mcp.json`, runtime-discovered, **and the host's live manager** so ACP client-declared servers from `session/new` resolve), the anonymous connection probe, OAuth endpoint discovery, client-credential assembly (configured > persisted > stored > metadata-advertised, DCR preferred), the browser flow itself (single-flight claim, login raced against host abort, 5-minute deadline that tears the flow down, normalized client secrets so a DCR confidential client's secret actually reaches the token exchange), and the persistence policy (url-keyed credential row, `auth` block pointer, only user-supplied secrets written back, definition-only entries stay clean). The TUI controller keeps only its presentation (transcript blocks, clipboard, manual input, Esc — restored only while still owning the hook); the ACP/text dispatcher keeps plain-text output — the URL is emitted as text since OSC 52 escapes would corrupt the JSON-RPC stream, and there's no composer over ACP for manual code input.

Host wiring: the host abort signal is wired before the anonymous probe so the whole reauth is cancellable; RPC dispatches through `runCommandInBackground` with a per-prompt AbortController that host abort, `abort_and_prompt`, `abort_and_restore_queue`, and stdin EOF all fire, so a backgrounded browser wait never parks the serialized queue or the shutdown drain; print mode routes slash input through the shared dispatcher before `session.prompt()` (previously the literal text went to the model), with diagnostics on stderr; and ACP reconnects the live manager's server after a successful reauth via a `reconnectMcpServer` runtime hook, with the manager now bound to the session auth storage so the fresh url-keyed row actually resolves. `unauth`/`smithery-login`/`smithery-logout`/`reconnect` stay TUI-only since they need live-manager UI actions, not a browser.

## Why

emacs users driving omp through agent-shell (and Zed, or `omp -p`) currently cannot recover from an expired OAuth token: the server sits unauthorized and the only fix is opening a separate TUI session or hand-editing credentials. The refusal had no technical basis — the browser launch and callback server work identically regardless of which client owns the stdio pipe.

Related (separate, already-open PR that this builds on top of in daily use but does not depend on): #15885.

## Testing

- `bun run check:types` (tsgo) clean; `bunx oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean on all touched files.
- ACP suite (`test/mcp-command-reauth-acp.test.ts`, 7 tests): reauthorize + persist with the TUI's policy (legacy credential GC, raw `${...}` placeholder preserved), definition-only no-write-back, stdio guidance + unknown name, anonymous-connection refusal, a real-`login` DCR test (stubbed HTTP for registration/token, real local callback server driven like a browser redirect) asserting the DCR-issued `client_secret` reaches the token exchange and is embedded in the credential row but never the config file — verified to fail against the pre-fix normalization — an abort-mid-flow test asserting the cancelled path writes no credential, and a client-declared-server test asserting `runtime.mcpManager` lookups reauth servers that live in no config file.
- TUI suites unchanged and green: `mcp-command-reauth` (22), `mcp-discovered-server-reauth`, `mcp-command-reload-status`, `mcp-command-toggle`, `mcp-name-autocomplete`, `acp-agent`, `acp-builtins`, `slash-commands`, `print-persistence-failure`, `noninteractive-dispose` (1177 tests across affected surfaces).
- Wire smoke against a compiled binary over real ACP stdio: `session/new` + `session/prompt` with `/mcp reauth local` (stdio server fixture) reached the engine guidance instead of the TUI-only refusal.

---

selected_prs.title: fix(task): relay a woken subagent's final report, not all its turn text
selected_prs.body:
## What

I made a woken subagent send back only its final answer, because it was gluing every bit of text from the turn together.

When an idle subagent is woken by an IRC message and answers in prose, the text relayed to the agent that woke it (and to the parent's wake job) was every text block of every assistant message in that turn, joined with no separator. A turn that says `Checking.`, calls `read`, then says `Answer.` relayed `Checking.Answer.`; with this PR it relays `Answer.`.

The wake path now picks its text with `lastReportTurnText()`, the same selection a first-run message result already uses (`finalizeRunResult`): the prose of the last assistant message that started no further work.

## Why

`attachIrcWakeTurnMonitor` read `turnMonitor.rawOutput()`, which is `finalOutputChunks.join("")` over the whole turn. The first-run path moved off `rawOutput()` for message results; the wake relay never did, so narration before tool calls ran straight into the answer for both peer relays (`relayWakeTurnOutput`) and the parent's wake-job result (`buildWakeRelayBody`).

Decisions:
- The `lastAssistantSalvageText()` fallback (the session's last assistant text, `main`'s source when the turn had no chunks) now applies only when the monitor saw no assistant message in the turn. A turn it did see never falls back: that text can be narration `lastReportTurnText()` set aside, such as prose before a Cursor-resolved call with nothing after it, and the turn gets the existing "produced no output" notice instead.
- Structured first runs (`task.structured: true`) still finalize from `rawOutput()` when they don't yield; that path is untouched here.

Non-goals: the yielded path (it relays the `<task-result>` summary) and failure notices are unchanged.

## Testing

Two tests in `test/task/executor-result-acceptance.test.ts`, each a peer waking an idle subagent:
- The turn emits `[text "Checking." + read toolCall]`, then `[text "Answer."]`; the peer receives `Answer.`. With the `executor.ts` change reverted it fails: `Expected: "Answer." Received: "Checking.Answer."`.
- The turn ends on `[text "Running the tests." + Cursor-resolved bash call]`; the peer gets the "produced no output" notice, not the narration. With the fallback applied unconditionally it fails (`Received: "Running the tests."`).

Existing relay tests that drive only the session's last assistant message (`persisted-revive.test.ts`, `irc.test.ts`) still pass.

Live, with Haiku: a parent messaged an idle subagent that had to read `notes.txt` for a secret word. On `main` the reply was `I'll read notes.txt to find the secret word.MARMALADE`; with the fix it was `MARMALADE` (2 of 2 runs). That run's build applied the salvage fallback unconditionally, its only difference from this head; the scenario has a report turn, so it never reaches the fallback.

```sh
cd packages/coding-agent && bun test test/task/executor-result-acceptance.test.ts test/task/executor-irc-wake-yield-reset.test.ts
```

selected_prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep a warm-revived subagent's peer roster as it last saw it
selected_prs.body:
## What

Waking a parked subagent re-sent its whole conversation uncached, because the revived session re-rendered the peer roster at the end of its system prompt, so I made the revive show the roster the agent last saw and refresh it on later rebuilds as a live agent does.

The first request after a revival now reads the whole cached prompt: in a live Haiku run it wrote 1,274 → 110 tokens to the cache. The saved write is everything after the roster, so it grows with the conversation; one real Opus revival wrote 254,328 tokens and read 0.

- `task/executor.ts`: each prompt render records the roster it shows; when a session is disposed, the roster its base prompt holds is kept (`ircRoster`). While `createWarmSubagentReviver` rebuilds the session (`reviving`), the prompt builder renders that roster instead of the registry's.

Closes #15523

## Why

A parked subagent is rebuilt from its spawn spec when a message wakes it. The prompt's `# Peers` block lists live peers with status and activity plus a parked count, and the rebuild read them from the registry at that moment. Peers almost always change while an agent sleeps, so the revived system prompt differed near its end and nothing past it was cached; on Anthropic each revival re-wrote the full conversation at cache-write price.

**Decision:** the revived agent sees the roster it last saw, as it would had it stayed live: a live subagent's prompt keeps its roster until something rebuilds it. Changed peers stay discoverable through `history://`, which the prompt points to, and any later rebuild renders the live roster. Rejected: a roster-delta reminder on revival, a new delivery path that tells a revived agent more than a live one gets.

Non-goal: tools an extension registers only from `before_agent_start` still don't come back on revival, so a revived agent using such a plugin still misses the cache.

## Testing

- New `persisted-revive.test.ts` cases, each a `runSubprocess` spawn with the real prompt builder, then a warm revive through `ensureLive`:
  - a running peer registers while the subagent is parked: the revived request's system blocks equal the spawn's last request, and a later `refreshBaseSystemPrompt` shows the peer. With the fix reverted it fails on the `# Peers` block.
  - a rebuild that renders a new peer is discarded (`refreshBaseSystemPrompt(() => false)`) and the peer leaves before the revive: the revived request still equals the last one sent, with no ghost peer.
  - a `before_agent_start` hook merges every block into one and a peer joins while parked: the revived request still equals the last one sent.
- `bun test test/task/persisted-revive.test.ts`: 45 pass; `bun run check` in `packages/coding-agent` passes.
- Live, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`, `task.agentIdleTtlMs: 5000`, `--no-extensions`: the main agent spawns subagent Probe, waits until it parks, spawns Other and waits until it parks, then messages Probe. Probe's first revived request:

| | cache read | cache write | revived prompt |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 18,197 | 1,274 | spawn's plus `1 parked peer(s) omitted.` |
| this PR | 19,342 | 110 | spawn's (no new `session_init` recorded) |
