selected_prs.title: fix(chat-runtime): harden the ACP harness against agent crashes, hangs and lost resumes
selected_prs.body: **Links** - Audit: https://app.superset.sh/page/acp-chat-what-needs-fixing-q5nxax (this PR covers items 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and 8) ## Summary - A crash mid-turn now fails the turn, instead of leaving it "running" forever in the journal. - A resume only falls back to a new session when the agent says the session is missing. Other load failures end the session dead, and the renderer retries the resume. - Startup and short requests time out. Agent stderr is shown and logged. Stop answers open approvals. The agent's whole process group is killed on exit or close. ## Why / Context ACP is the only path for new chats (`packages/chat/src/core/harness/harness.ts:10`). Its protocol mapping is well tested, but the process lifecycle around it was not. Each of these was a real failure mode: 1. **Crash mid-turn.** `AcpRpcClient.handleExit` rejects the pending `session/prompt`, then calls `onExit` at once, which closes the event queue. The "failed" turn from `runTurn`'s `catch` came a microtask later, and the closed queue dropped it. 2. **Resume.** Any `session/load` error fell back to `session/new` with an info notice. A transient or auth error during resume replaced the conversation the agent knew. The transcript was still in chat.db, but the agent had lost the context. 3. **No timeouts.** A CLI blocked on a keychain or OAuth prompt left the chat "starting" forever. The dead-session recovery never ran. 4. **Stderr.** It was discarded, so every crash read only `acp agent exited (code 1)`. 5. **Approvals on Stop.** The ACP spec requires the client to answer pending `request_permission` requests as cancelled. An agent that waits on that answer never ended the turn. 6. **Orphaned processes.** `close()` sent SIGKILL only to the adapter's node process. The `claude`/`codex` CLI under it could outlive the chat. A spawn failure (for example, a deleted cwd) or an EPIPE only reached the host's global uncaught-exception handler. ## How It Works - `AcpAdapter.handleExit` emits a `failed` turn for a running turn before it closes the queue. - `sessionMissing()` accepts -32002 (claude-agent-acp maps "No conversation found" to it). It also accepts only session-specific messages ("unknown sessionId", "session not found", "no conversation found", "no rollout found"), so "model not found" keeps the resume: pi-acp answers -32602 `Unknown sessionId`, and codex-acp answers "no rollout found for thread id". I checked these in the pinned adapter sources. - Any other failure throws "Could not reopen this conversation…". - The session ends dead, and `AcpChatPane` recovers it with its existing bounded retries (`MAX_RECOVERIES`, backoff), then shows the manual retry panel. - `AcpRpcClient.request` takes an optional `timeoutMs` and rejects with `AcpTimeoutError`. - Startup (`initialize`, `session/load`, `session/new`): 120 s. - Mode, config option, fork and background stop: 30 s. - `session/prompt` and steering have no deadline. A steer that timed out went back on the queue, so a late answer from the agent ran the prompt twice. - Both are adapter options, so tests use small values. When startup fails, the client is closed. - The last 4 KB of stderr is kept, logged with `console.warn` on exit, and added to the exit and startup error notices. - `spawnAcpTransport`: - spawns `detached` (its own process group) on non-Windows, and SIGKILLs the group on exit and when the close grace period runs out. - has `error` listeners on the child and stdin. - reports exit on `close`, with a 500 ms fallback after `exit`, so stdout is read to the end first. ## Manual QA Checklist Not done in the running app yet. Before merging, I'd check: - [ ] Claude chat: send a prompt, then `kill -9` the adapter process mid-turn. The turn shows failed and the recovery panel appears. - [ ] After that, no `claude` process from that chat is left (`ps -o pid,pgid,command`). - [ ] Restart host-service with a chat open. It resumes with history, not "No earlier conversation to open". - [ ] Open an approval, press Stop. The approval goes stale and the turn ends. - [ ] Break auth (log out of the CLI) and open a new chat. The error notice shows the agent's stderr. ## Testing - `bun test` in `packages/chat-runtime`: 249 pass. - `bun test src/chat-v3` in `packages/host-service`: 30 pass. - `bun run typecheck` in `packages/chat-runtime`: clean. Host-service typecheck has 21 errors, all in `../trpc`, from packages that aren't built in a fresh worktree; none are in changed files. - `biome check` on the changed directory: clean. - 8 new tests. Seven fail on the old code; the "unknown session id falls back" one is a guard that passes on both. - The 6 adapter tests use the fake agent. - The 2 `spawnAcpTransport` tests start a real child process: one checks that the agent's own child is killed on close, one that a missing command reports an exit. They run in about 70 ms and are skipped on Windows. ## Risks / Rollout - **Process groups.** A detached agent no longer gets Ctrl+C from a terminal running host-service in dev. It still exits on stdin EOF, and the group kill reaps it on close. - **Resume classification.** If an adapter reports a missing session with an error we don't recognise, that chat goes dead and the renderer retries a few times, instead of opening a new session. Before, a missing session always opened a new one. - **Timeouts.** A very large `session/load` replay that takes longer than 120 s will now fail. It is retried by the renderer. - **Claude crash during resume.** claude-agent-acp 0.85.0 also maps "Query closed before response received" (the CLI died while resuming) to -32002 (`acp-agent.js:6803`). For Claude, that case still opens a new session. Fixing it needs an upstream change. - **Background processes.** The group kill also ends processes the agent started in the background, such as a dev server from a Bash tool, when its chat closes or the agent dies. Closing a terminal agent's pane does the same through SIGHUP. A process that calls `setsid` itself escapes it. - **Rollback:** revert this commit. There are no data or protocol changes. ## Review follow-up (4e1fa63e9b) - `LiveSession` discards queued prompts when the session goes dead. Before, a crash's failed turn handed the next queued prompt to the dead adapter, and the chat stayed "running". There is a new test, which fails without the fix. - The missing-session match is narrowed, and the test now uses "model not found". - A broken stdin pipe kills the agent, so pending requests fail instead of hanging. - The stderr tail is logged once on a startup failure, and timeouts under a second are shown in ms. ## Follow-ups (from the audit, not in this PR) - Idle reaping and a per-host limit on live chat sessions. - Fall back to the terminal agent when the CLI is missing or too old, not only when the harness is missing. - Run `acp-smoke` against the user-installed CLI on a schedule, and add a version gate for pi. - Ship the adapters in the CLI host bundle, and treat a desktop resolve failure as an error. --- ## Summary by cubic Hardens the ACP harness so agent crashes, hangs, and failed resumes no longer leave chats stuck or silently replace context. - A mid-turn agent crash now fails the turn and marks the session dead instead of leaving it "running" forever in the journal. Queued prompts are discarded when the session dies, so a waiting prompt no longer holds the session at "running". - A resume only starts a new session when the agent reports the session as missing; any other load failure ends the session dead and lets the renderer retry. - Startup requests (initialize, session load/new) time out after 120s; mode, option, fork, and stop requests after 30s. Steering has no deadline, since a late answer after a timeout ran the steered prompt twice. The agent is closed when startup fails, and close errors are logged instead of surfacing as unhandled rejections. - The last 4 KB of agent stderr is logged on exit and included in error notices. - Stopping a turn now answers pending permission requests as cancelled, per the ACP spec. - The agent spawns in its own process group, which is SIGKILLed on exit or close so agent CLI children don't outlive their chat. Spawn and stdin errors are handled instead of reaching the process-wide uncaught-exception handler. **Risks / rollout** - A detached agent no longer receives Ctrl+C from a dev terminal; it still exits on stdin EOF. - An unrecognized "session missing" error from an adapter now leaves the chat dead (with retries) rather than silently opening a new session. - A session load replay longer than 120s now times out; the renderer retries. - Rollback is a single revert; no data or protocol changes. Written for commit 4a3653e7c8e0cb554d0cf0464c7eacfc8ad9297d. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * ACP requests now time out instead of waiting indefinitely, with configurable startup and request time limits. * Startup and process-exit errors include available diagnostic output. * Resuming a session opens a new session only when the requested session is missing; other loading errors are reported. * Stopping a turn cancels pending permission approvals. If the agent exits mid-turn, the turn is marked as failed. * Agent processes are cleaned up when the connection closes, and launch errors are surfaced more reliably. * Prompts queued when a session becomes unavailable are discarded instead of being sent.

selected_prs.title: feat(tasks): filter task lists by exact labels
selected_prs.body:
Refs #8454 (the exact label filter part; hierarchy and sidebar are not in this PR).

## Problem
There is no way to list tasks with a given label. `--search acme` also matches titles and descriptions. The query layer already had an exact label filter (`TaskListFilters.labels`), but `taskListFilterSchema` had no `labels` field, so zod dropped it.

## Change
- `task.list` / `task.listPage`: optional `labels: string[]` (max 20), passed to `buildTaskListConditions`. A task must have every label; names are trimmed and lowercased. Optional field, so released clients are unaffected.
- CLI: `superset tasks list --labels acme,client-one`. Rejected for `--tracker linear`.
- MCP `tasks_list`: `labels` input, rejected for Linear.
- SDK `TaskListParams.labels`, CLI and SDK docs.

The desktop Tasks view still filters on the client; moving it to the server filter is a follow-up.

## Tests
- `list.test.ts` calls `task.list` and `task.listPage` and checks that each label reaches the query (trimmed, lowercased), and that a label of only spaces is rejected. Both tests fail without the change.
- End to end against a local API on a worktree Neon branch, with the built CLI, the `/mcp` endpoint and the SDK:
  - `--labels acme` returns only tasks with that label; a task that only mentions "acme" in its title is not returned (`--search acme` returns it).
  - `--labels acme,client-one` requires both. `" ACME , Client-One "` matches the same. An unknown label returns nothing.
  - Combines with `--assignee-me`. `--labels ","` applies no filter.
  - `task.listPage` (desktop path) and MCP `tasks_list` filter the same way. SDK `tasks.list({ labels })` works.
  - `--tracker linear --labels` and MCP `tracker: "linear"` with labels are rejected.
  - 21 labels and `""` are rejected. A call without `labels` returns the same rows as before.
- `bun test` in `packages/trpc` passes. Typecheck shows no errors in changed files.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Filter Superset tasks by labels when listing them through the CLI, SDK, and task tools. Provide one or more labels; tasks must match all specified labels.
  * Label matching is exact and ignores capitalization in the task tools. The CLI accepts comma-separated labels and ignores extra whitespace.
* **Limitations**
  * Label filtering is not supported for Linear task listings.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

selected_prs.title: feat(tasks): label hierarchy with path names and a label filter in the Tasks view
selected_prs.body: Refs #8454 (label hierarchy and grouping by company and project). ## What changes - **Path labels.** A label named `acme/website` creates its parents (`acme`) and links each label to its parent through `task_labels.parent_id`. Names stay unique per organization, so there is no migration, and clients that match labels by name keep working. `normalizeLabelName` trims each segment, so `Acme / Website` becomes `acme/website`. - **Filter includes sub-labels.** The `labels` filter on `task.list` and `task.listPage` (from #8458) now matches a label and its sub-labels, so `acme` returns tasks labelled `acme/website`. A name prefix does not match: `acm` returns nothing. CLI `--labels`, MCP `tasks_list`, and the docs say so. - **Desktop Tasks view: Label filter.** A new top-bar filter shows the labels as a tree and filters on the server, so it covers every task and not only the loaded pages. It is in the URL (`?label=`), kept when opening a task and going back, and when leaving Tasks and coming back through the sidebar. - **Label picker.** Sub-labels are indented under their parent. The Create item stays visible when the typed path has spaces around the slash; before, cmdk's fuzzy match hid it and nothing could be created. The sidebar of companies and projects from the issue is not in this PR. The Label filter covers the same navigation. ## Tests - Unit: `ensureLabels` creates and links parents (new `labels.test.ts`), the SQL matches sub-labels with LIKE escaped (`task-list-query.test.ts`), the routers forward labels (`list.test.ts`), and path helpers and tree order (`packages/shared/src/labels.test.ts`). The new server tests fail on `main`. - End to end on a local API and the dev desktop over CDP. Screenshots are on the Superset page linked in the comments. - Seeded 9 tasks through `task.create` with path labels. The DB shows each label linked to its parent, 3 levels deep for `globex/platform/api`. - `listPage` with `acme` returns all 5 Acme tasks, `acme/website` returns 2, `globex/platform` returns 1, and `acm` returns 0. - In the app, choosing `acme`, then `acme/website`, then `globex` (board view) shows the right tasks. "All labels" clears the filter. The filter is kept when opening a task and going back, and through a sidebar round trip. - Created `Acme / Design` from the task's label picker. It saved as `acme/design` and is linked to `acme`. - No console errors during the flow. - `bun test`: shared, db, trpc, mcp, cli, i18n, and the desktop dashboard all pass. `check:i18n` passes, with translations for all 16 locales. The filter button's "Label" has its own context, because the existing "Label" string means a field name. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds label hierarchy with path names and a server-side Label filter in the desktop Tasks view (refs #8454). **New Features** - A label named `acme/web` creates its parents (`acme`) and links each label to its parent via `task_labels.parent_id`; names stay unique per organization, so no migration is needed. - Creating a path label runs in a transaction, so a failure can't leave a partial label tree. - `normalizeLabelName` trims each segment, so `Acme / Website` becomes `acme/website`. - The `labels` filter on `task.list` and `task.listPage` matches a label, its sub-labels, and the stored name of labels saved before normalization. `acme` returns tasks labelled `acme/website`, but `acm` matches nothing; a filter that cannot be a label (over 64 characters, or only slashes) matches nothing instead of being dropped. - The Tasks view's Label filter shows labels as a tree, filters server-side, and persists in the URL (`?label=`). - Sub-labels are indented in the label picker, and the Create item stays visible when the typed path has spaces around the slash. - The company/project sidebar from the issue is not included; the Label filter covers that navigation. Written for commit 0a40a3dfd14ad5a2e3cd920b4a3ea47b9fb5e967. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Filter tasks by label with searchable selection and nested labels displayed in a hierarchy. * Preserve the selected label when navigating between the task list and task details, and when creating tasks. * Label filters match the selected label and its sub-labels, ignoring letter case and surrounding spaces. * **Documentation** * Clarified that task label filters match sub-labels as well as exact labels.

selected_prs.title: feat(desktop, chat): center pane area for terminals and chats, /mcp picker, edit a sent message, and ACP sessions API + CLI
selected_prs.body:
This PR consolidates several pieces of work so they ship together:

| Part | Author | What |
|---|---|---|
| A | @saddlepaddle | Center pane area holds terminals and chats; smoother right sidebar |
| B | @AviPeltz | `/mcp` picker in the chat composer (was #8578) |
| C | Harshith | Edit a sent message (replaces `/rewind`), tool-run transcript, ACP sessions API + CLI with automation routing, chat history picker |

---

## A. Center pane area and right sidebar (@saddlepaddle)

With `right-pane-area` on, the center pane area only holds terminals and chats. Everything else opens on the right. The right sidebar also animates and resizes smoothly, without rebuilding its panes.

### Part 1: Pane placement (flag on)

#### Why
The right pane area replaces the old files/changes sidebar. The center is for working sessions; viewers belong beside them.

#### What / How
- A `PaneTarget { store, reveal }` replaces raw stores in the openers (`useWorkspacePaneOpeners`, `useWorkspaceFileNavigation`, `useWorkspaceHotkeys`, deep links, activity menu, subagent opens). `page.tsx` points that viewer target at the right store when the flag is on, else at the center.
- `moveViewerPanesToRight` runs on load and on every center change. It moves any non-terminal, non-chat pane into its own right tab. Tabs that mix kinds are split apart.
- Terminal, page, file and chat link clicks always land on the right when the right area exists, so the "Open in right pane" modifier now matches a plain click.
- Center "+" menu: **Terminal** and **Chat** only. Chat opens with the last-used chat agent (see Part 5); you switch agent in the new chat screen. Desktop moves to the right "+" menu (sandboxes only).
- Removed: **Move to Center**, **Merge into center**.
- The right sidebar closes itself when its last tab closes.

#### Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘⇧J (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+J) | New Chat (Chat category, next to ⌘J Focus Chat Input) |

⌘⇧T stays free for a future v2 reopen-closed-tab.

### Part 2: Right-area opening rules

`createWorkspaceStore({ placePane })` in `@superset/panes`, with `openPane({ pane, beside? })`. The center keeps its behaviour (split beside the anchor or the active pane); the right store passes `placeInTabs`. Opening a pane on the right:
1. If the item is already open, focus that tab (each opener checks this first).
2. Else replace an unpinned pane of the same kind in any tab (preview behavior; double-click still pins).
3. Else add a tab.

It never splits by itself. `openBesidePane` (the Files, Changes, Review and Pages lists) and the "open Changes in a pane" setting follow the same rules. Users can still split with the split button, the right-click menu, or drag and drop.

### Part 3: Sidebar motion and performance (all users unless noted)

#### Separator drags (measured over CDP in a dev build)
Every drag frame used to re-render the whole left workspace list.
- **Right:** the width was saved each frame to `v2UserPreferences`, which about 19 hooks watch. That includes `useTagFolderContext` in every sidebar row.
- **Left:** `DashboardLayout` subscribed to the whole sidebar store, and its providers handed fresh values to every row.

Fixes:
- `ResizablePanel` `commitOnRelease` tracks the width locally and saves it on release.
- The left width moved into `WorkspaceSidebarPanel`, its only subscriber. That is what fixed the left drag: the sidebar is passed in as `children`, so React skips it when the panel re-renders. `DashboardSidebar` is also memoized, which only saves re-renders when `DashboardLayout` re-renders for other reasons.

Result: **75–83 ms → 8.3 ms per frame**, no long tasks, on both sides.

#### Open / close / expand (`SidebarSlide`), modelled on Codex's split view
- The panel is anchored to the window's right edge and uses one element tree in every mode, so switching modes never remounts panes. Transitions run 300 ms `ease`, with `contain: strict` while moving.
- **Open/close** animate the space taken from the center on the same curve, so the center follows the panel edge and the composer never cuts off and then jumps.
- **Expand** overlays the center, which stays mounted and `inert`, instead of moving tabs. Content resizes with the panel. The persisted `rightPaneAreaExpansion` snapshot and `expandPaneArea` are deleted.
- **Flag on only:** after the first open, the right area stays mounted while closed (invisible and `inert`). Terminals keep running and browser pages stay loaded. It deliberately doesn't use React `<Activity>`, which would run effect cleanups and detach terminals.
- **Browser panes:** their webviews are hoisted to `<body>`, so `browserRuntimeRegistry.relayout()` now clips each one to its clipping ancestors (`visibleClipPath`) and parks it when hidden. The slide calls it on every frame.

#### Manual QA (dev app, driven over CDP)
- [x] Separator drag, both sides: 8.3 ms p50 per frame, no long tasks.
- [x] Open/close/expand/restore: no long tasks in the clean run. The right-area DOM survives every transition. Filmstrips show no cut-then-jump.
- [x] Terminal in the right area: exactly 1 SIGWINCH per expand and per restore, 0 for close/reopen.
- [x] Browser pane in the right area: clipped during the slide, parked while closed, follows expand/restore, same `webContentsId` throughout.
- [x] Closing the last right tab auto-closes the sidebar.
- [x] 7 rapid toggles and 5 rapid expands settle in the right state, with no errors.
- [x] `inert` blocks focus into the closed right area and into the covered center.
- [x] Flag off: the old sidebar opens and closes, renders correctly, no errors, and unmounts when closed.
- [ ] `placePane` clicking through files in the Files tree (unit-tested only; not driven in the app)
- [ ] Packaged build

#### Testing
- `bun run typecheck` (desktop): clean apart from existing better-auth session-type errors in `_authenticated/layout.tsx` and friends, which aren't from this PR.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` + `bun test` in `packages/panes`: 123/123.
- `bun test src/renderer` (desktop): 6846 pass, 1 fail. The failure is in `useComposerDictation`, a Lexical `HISTORY_MERGE_TAG` import-order error that also fails on its own and isn't touched here.
- `bunx biome check`: clean. `bun run check:i18n`: 0 missing.
- New tests: `SidebarSlide` (modes, no remount, keep mounted, rapid toggles); right-store placement rules; `visibleClipPath`; `moveViewerPanesToRight`; `subscribePaneAreaEmptied`; updated link-action and forwarded-hotkey tests.

#### Known Limitations
- With the flag off, the old sidebar has an 80–180 ms long task on each toggle. No baseline was measured, so it may predate this PR.
- While expanded, center shortcuts (e.g. ⌘T) still target the hidden center store.
- A browser's "open in new window" still splits, because it uses the same split action as the button.

#### Rollback
Revert the commit. The removed persisted `rightPaneAreaExpansion` field is optional, so older builds read rows without it.

---

## B. `/mcp` picker (@AviPeltz, from #8578, reworked in review)

- `/mcp` in the chat composer opens a searchable list of the MCP servers the chat's agent has in this workspace. A pick becomes a chip. Typing `/mcp` and pressing Enter opens the same picker.
- On send, the hint naming the picked servers goes to the agent as a **hidden content part**. The stored and shown message is exactly what the user typed (bubble, Copy, Edit). Hidden parts reach the agent wrapped in `<superset-context>`, so a replay of the agent's history (session/load) drops them again.
- Superset plugin servers that aren't installed or have no connected account show **Install** / **Connect**. Connect uses the Plugins page's connect-first flow (`ConnectConnectorDialog connectOnly` → `useInstallAfterConnect`), so a plugin is installed only after its account is connected.
- Host query `agentTooling.listMcpServers` reads Claude Code and Codex config files for a workspace (files only; nothing is started or contacted). It returns `{ servers, supported }`; each server is config only (`name`, `agent`, `scope`, `transport`, `url`, `configPath`, `state`). The desktop joins it with the plugin catalog: a proxied server is matched to its plugin by its `/mcp/plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>` URL, others by name or endpoint.
- A message replayed from the agent's history has no recorded chip elements, so `@mcp/` tokens and a leading `/command` become chips from the text.

---

## C. Editing, transcript, sessions API (Harshith)

### Edit a sent message (replaces `/rewind`)
- Hover a user message → **Edit**. Sending the edit rewinds the **conversation only**: the chat continues in a new session holding the transcript before that message, and the edited message is sent. Files are never touched (the earlier checkpoint/restore design was removed).
- **Claude, Codex and pdev fork natively** at the last reply before the message (`session/fork` with a cut point), and the fork is resumed quietly.
- **Other agents** get the earlier conversation as a hidden part of the same prompt as the edited message, so there is no extra acknowledgement turn. The rewound session is seeded with the earlier events, so nothing is parsed back out of our own prompt text.

### Transcript: tool runs
- A run of tool calls stays folded ("Ran 3 commands") while the agent works, as in #8339. The step still running shows under the fold with its command and a ticking timer: `Running bun test 42s`. The summary counts only finished steps, so it never says "Ran" about something still running. (Follows the "Why the chat feels slow while the agent works" page.)
- The agent's thinking between tool calls folds into the run, in order. A run that stays one call is still a plain row.
- The "Working for…" clock sits under the latest prompt of the turn, so a message steered in mid-turn shows the live indicator below it.

### ACP sessions API and `superset sessions` CLI
- Host `sessions.*`: `capabilities`, `create`, `list`, `get`, `read`, `send`, `resume`, `close`. No host-side feature-flag check: the desktop UI and automation dispatch keep their `acp-chat` gates, and no host call depends on an API round trip.
- CLI: `superset sessions create` (new chats only), `import --agent --native-session` (adopt a session the agent started outside Superset), `resume`, `send` (resumes a stopped chat first and reports the session the prompt went to), `read` (prints the cursor for older events), `list`, `close`, `open`.
- Automation dispatch launches through `launchAgentSession`: `sessions.create` for agents the host can chat with, `agents.run` otherwise or on hosts without `sessions`. Chat runs are recorded as `chat` with their session id, and run links carry `?sessionId=` so they open the chat. New cloud boxes launch on first boot and report back with `reportCloudLaunch`.

### Other chat changes
- Provider-scoped chat history picker: saved chats plus the agent's own sessions (`discoverSessions`); an older host without it shows "not supported".
- The CLI | Chat surface toggle is removed.
- New chats (center "+" → Chat, ⌘⇧J) open the last-used chat agent.
- Agent failures are no longer silent: a turn that ends with no output shows an error notice, and recovery shows a dead session's real error via `getSession`'s `lastError`.
- Switching provider in a chat with history offers **Start fresh** or **Fork conversation**.

### API compatibility
- New host procedures are unreleased: `sessions.*`, `agentTooling.listMcpServers`, chat `rewindSession`, `discoverSessions`. Clients fall back on hosts without them (`agents.run` for dispatch, "not supported" in the history picker).
- Additive fields only on existing shapes: optional `hidden` on text content parts, `agentMessageId` on agent messages and `lastError` on `getSession`.

---

## Testing
- `bun test` (bun 1.4.3): trpc 674, cli 438, shared 1432, chat 83, chat-runtime 301, chat-ui 34, panes 121, desktop v2-workspace 800, all pass.
- host-service: 2603 pass, 2 fail on the 5 s timeout under machine load (terminal disposal, which also fails on clean `main` locally; `getGitStatusPartial` convergence, in code this PR doesn't change).
- Typecheck clean for desktop, host-service, cli, chat, chat-runtime, chat-ui, shared, panes, apart from existing better-auth session-type errors. `bun run lint:fix` clean. `bun run check:i18n`: 0 missing.

## Manual QA (dev app over CDP, Claude and pdev)
- [x] Folded run with the running step and timer under it ("Ran 1 command" / `Running sleep 15 && echo done 5s`); finished runs fold; nothing opens or closes while the agent works
- [x] Thinking folds into runs; "Working for" sits under a steered message
- [x] `/mcp`: hint never in the bubble, also after a restart replays the agent's history; replayed `@mcp/` tokens render as chips; typed `/mcp` + Enter opens the picker; proxied plugin servers without an account show **Connect**
- [x] Connection notice ("Starting the agent…") aligned with the composer text
- [ ] Edit with the new one-prompt rewind (unit-tested; driven in the app before that change)
- [ ] `placePane` on the right (unit-tested only)
- [ ] Codex live; packaged build

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Cloud dispatch: provision, wait for the host to come online, then launch through the same `launchAgentSession` path, replacing `reportCloudLaunch`.
- One dispatch pipeline: resolve target → `HostCaller` + workspace → `launchAgentSession` → `recordDispatchedRun`.
- Chat runtime: one ACP connection per agent per workspace, panes bound to a chat id.

selected_prs.title: fix(cloud): attribute every usage event to its boot, workspace and user
selected_prs.body:
## Why

Autumn's total for the Superset org reconciles exactly with what the meter billed (40,558 GB-minutes as of 06:30 UTC today), but its per-user and per-boot groupings are wrong: every user shows negative usage. The balance lock taken at boot and on each 30-minute renewal carried no properties, so only the confirm deltas were attributed and each user's group equals their billed usage minus every hold taken on their boxes.

Two boxes running since before the cutover were also never adopted because Vercel's tag-filtered listing paginates in creation order (commit `ec5d0a75c0`), and settlement stopped looking after one page of sessions.

## What

- Put `bootId`, `lockSeq`, `workspaceId`, `userId` and `meteringVersion: 1` on the lock itself so confirms inherit the attribution. CPU events get the same properties; a failed CPU track now fails the settle so it retries instead of being dropped.
- List sandboxes by status time without the server-side tag filter, and walk every page of sessions when settling a boot.
- `packages/trpc/scripts/audit-cloud-metering.ts` compares an org's Autumn events against the Vercel sessions behind them.

Usage recorded before this ships is re-attributed separately, outside this PR.

## Verification

- `bun test` for `meter.test.ts` and `vercel.test.ts`: 27 pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/trpc`, plus the audit script under a temporary tsconfig: clean.
- Cross-checked production: Vercel sessions (via the sandbox SDK), `cloud_workspace_boots`, and Autumn events for the Superset org. Every session started after the cutover has a boot whose runtime matches Vercel's; the per-user shortfall equals the number of confirmed holds times the hold size for all four users.

selected_prs.title: feat(gui-app): offer Open as chat on a subagent card that only replied
selected_prs.body:
## What

"Open as chat" is offered on every subagent card, including one whose subagent only replied.

The control in a subagent card's header was drawn only when the card had nested activity. The read-only view it opens is where **Continue as chat** lives, so a subagent that answered without calling a tool could not be continued from the GUI at all. Of everything around "Continue as chat" this was the case a user was most likely to meet.

## Change

| Card | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagent card with nested activity | control drawn | control drawn |
| Subagent card with no nested activity (it only replied, or has not produced anything yet) | no control | control drawn; the view shows the task, the result and Continue |
| Workflow card with nested activity | control drawn | control drawn |
| Workflow card with no nested activity | no control | no control |

`useOpenAsChatHeaderAction` no longer returns `null` for a card with no nested activity. The card shells still round the header's corner on `headerAction === null`, which now happens only when no transcript is in context.

The view needed no change: `SubagentChatBody` already renders the task, the result (when the conversation has no text of its own) and an empty-state line for a card with neither.

## Decisions

- **A workflow card keeps the nested-activity rule** (`useWorkflowOpenAsChatHeaderAction`). A workflow run is a fleet, not one conversation: its view has no task and no result, Continue is never offered for it (`card.workflowMeta === null` in `useSubagentContinueAsChat`), so with no activity it would open an empty page.
- **A card still streaming with no content gets the control.** Its view opens on the task, and Continue is disabled while the subagent runs (`isPending = requestPending || isStreaming`), as it already was for a streaming card with activity.

## Verification

- `subagent-segment.test.tsx`: each card variant (promoted, card, row) with no nested children draws `subagent-open-as-chat-<id>` and a click calls the opener with the card's id; no transcript context draws nothing; a workflow card draws none without children and draws it with children.
- `chat-message-assistant-body.test.tsx`: a reply-only promoted card inside a real assistant message draws the control and opens by its id.
- `subagent-chat-view.test.tsx`: a card with a task, a result and no children shows the task, the result and Continue, and Continue runs the action.
- Each new card case was seen red with the old `nested.length === 0` return restored, and the workflow cases red with the workflow guard removed.
- Three test files, 92 tests, pass. `lint:files` on the four files, `react-doctor --diff main` and the gui-app `compile` are clean.
- One cold review by a separate agent before the push: no findings.

The host side of the same work is traycerai/traycer-internal#6136; it does not depend on this change and this change does not depend on it.

selected_prs.title: feat(protocol,gui-app): chat.subscribe@1.28 marks a prompt held for a sign-in, and the GUI offers its cancel
selected_prs.body:
Built on `main` 4f2e2866. It no longer stacks on #2578. Its tree is `main` plus this change alone, and none of #2578's content remains. `main`'s `chat.subscribe` head is 1.27, so this PR opens 1.28.

The first version stacked on #2578 and opened 1.29. The branch was moved with a merge from `main`, not a force-push, so #2578's commits still show in the commit list. The diff against `main` is these 16 files only.

This is the OSS half of traycerai/traycer-internal#6533. That PR parks an agent's message when its provider is signed out instead of consuming it. Its host half sets the key below, and it moves the pin in its own turn.

## Why

A provider sign-out holds an agent's queued prompt until the sign-in returns. The prompt then runs unattended. The queue showed the held row with no control to stop it.

The GUI decides which controls a queued row gets from its `kind` and `sender.type` only. A received agent row gets no owner actions (`chat-queue-utils.ts` `isReceivedAgentResponse`, `queuedMessageRowChrome`). So no field the host could set would have produced a cancel.

## What

### Protocol: `chat.subscribe@1.28`

The live line adds one optional key, `signInParked`, on the queued prompt item. It adds no frame, union member or enum value. The host sets the key on a prompt it holds for a sign-in.

The posture is tolerance, not projection, as with `1.17`'s `sentFromHostId` on the same item:

- `1.17` through `1.27` bind a hand-frozen `chatQueuedPromptItemSchemaPreSignInParked`, closed and open alike.
- `1.27` freezes its snapshot queue and `queueChanged` on that copy.
- A peer below `1.28` drops the key as an unknown member and shows the row as before, with no cancel.
- A `1.28` client reading an older host's item finds no key and reads it as false.

The chores of opening a minor:

- 1.27 is frozen (`chatSubscribeServerFrameSchemaV127`), and `chatSubscribeV128` is registered.
- `latestMinor` moves in every suite that pins it.
- 1.27 is captured in `chat-schema-checkpoints.test.ts`.
- `chat-subscribe-line-surfaces.test.ts` pins the key on server frames from 1.28 only, and on no client frame.
- `chat-subscribe-sign-in-park-v128.test.ts` covers the tolerance: 1.28 keeps the key, an item without it reads as not parked, and 1.27 and 1.26 drop it.
- `clients/shared/host-transport` binds no `chat.subscribe` `ServerFrameSchemaV<N>`, and the CLI's `host-rpc.test.ts` identity check is derived from the registry. Neither needed a change.

### GUI

A received agent row that is paused and carries the mark gets the cancel-only toolbar that managed-command rows use. It has its own label, "Cancel agent message waiting for sign-in". No other agent row gets it. It sends the row's ordinary `queueCancel`, which the host admits for a held prompt.

## Decisions

- `signInParked` is `.optional()`, not `.default(false)`. This follows the precedent of the queue's `pausedReason` in `subscribe.ts`: a defaulted key is required on the inferred type, and the item is built as an object literal across the host, the GUI and their suites. On the wire both read the same, with an absent key read as false.

## Evidence

- **Frozen lines unchanged.** Every `chat.subscribe` line 1.0–1.27 has the same digests before and after the change on `main` 4f2e2866. That covers the server frame (input and output), the client frame and the open request. 1.28 differs from 1.27.
- **Red-first.** Three added rows in `queued-message-surface.test.tsx` were run against `main` 4f2e2866 before the change:
  - The cancel row fails: `Unable to find an accessible element with the role "button" and name "Cancel agent message waiting for sign-in"`.
  - The two guard rows pass there, as guards should: mark false or absent, and read-only.
  - All three pass at this head, and the whole file passes 81/81.
- **Local surface compatibility.** `check-protocol-compat.ts` reports this tree compatible with `main` 4f2e2866's surface.
- **Suites.** These passed at this head:
  - 52 protocol test files that touch `chat.subscribe` or the queue (2627 tests).
  - The commit hook: lint, format, affected compile and DCO.

selected_prs.title: feat(gui-app): a usage reading that could not load says so, and retries
selected_prs.body:
## What the person saw

Sentry user feedback DESKTOP-APP-1PQ, desktop 1.5.1 on macOS 26.5.2: "usage
limits not showing up". Case:
`automations/user-reports/cases/sentry-feedback-7801655278`.

Their Claude usage probe timed out eight times in thirteen minutes on a starved
machine (244 MiB free of 96 GiB). With nothing ever read for that account, the
host's gauge books the timeout itself as the reading
(`rate-limit-gauge-cache.ts:172-173` says so in as many words), and the strip
drew it in the `unavailable` state: the icon and a dash, whose documented
contract is "The provider answered and said it cannot report usage, which is a
fact about the account, not a blip"
(`status-bar-provider-segment.tsx:95-96`). The reason reached them only on
hover. Nothing was wrong with the account, and nothing said so.

## The state this adds

`segmentState` already had the right distinction one branch below: a transient
failure WITH a retained reading is `degraded`. It just had nowhere to put one
without. So `!available` splits on the reason:

| reason | state |
| --- | --- |
| `timeout`, `connection_failed`, `usage_fetch_failed` | `transient` |
| `rate_limits_not_available`, `insufficient_permissions`, `cli_not_found`, `sdk_incompatible`, `unsupported_provider`, `invalid_response` | `unavailable`, as before |

A read that REJECTED - the transport gave up, the frame budget ran out - is
the same state: nothing is retained, and "no reading yet" is then the one
sentence that is not true. It carries no wire reason, which the words do not
name anyway. `cold` stays what it was, the state before a first read. With
nothing retained the question is whether a read of that key has EVER rejected,
not whether it is rejected right now: a dataless query goes back to pending
while the retry runs, and the words would otherwise drop to an empty track for
the length of it.

Both of those are a read that CAN happen. An account whose credential is gone -
signed out, with its failure still in the cache - is kept on the strip on
purpose, and nothing anywhere reads it: not the poll, not the affordance, not
the scheduled re-read. So it keeps the state it had before this PR, and the
words with it: a transient wire reason is `unavailable`, which names the reason
and promises nothing, and a rejected read is `cold`, whose "no reading yet"
stays true while nothing is going to read one. That is the ACCOUNT's
eligibility, unmasked, and not what a placement may do. Three things mask what
a placement may pull - the usage region hidden, the provider deny-listed, the
layout editor drawing from cache - and none of them is a fact about the
account: the app-shell poll goes on reading it through every one of them, so a
segment reading the masked flag would say the account had answered while a read
of it was in flight, and say the opposite again when the mask lifted. The
account's own answer travels beside it as `accountReadable`, which no placement
touches.

That split is not written here. `@traycer/protocol`'s
`host/rate-limit/semantics.ts:23-30` owns it, because it is "load-bearing on
BOTH sides of the wire and must not drift"; `rate-limit-envelope.ts` already
imports the predicate for the `degraded` case. So no protocol minor, no method
bump, no tolerance question - the `reason` on `host.getRateLimitUsage` has
carried this all along and nothing on the wire moves.

## And no host change

The host already applies the one policy a retry has to respect, which is why
this is a GUI-only change:

- A person's click reads with `force: true`. That passes the two read floors
  (`provider-rate-limits.ts:121-122`, gated at `:347`) and NOTHING else: the
  read still joins one in flight for the same account, still takes the
  provider's usage-probe slot through `runProviderUsageProbe`, and Claude's
  refresh-safe 90s budget still applies where a credential may rotate.
- The automatic re-read goes out `force: false`, so those floors decide per
  reason whether anything is read at all. A `timeout` or `connection_failed`
  scope is past its 60s ephemeral floor and really reads again; a Claude
  `usage_fetch_failed` is inside the 15-minute penalty floor that exists
  because `/api/oauth/usage` answers a burst with a multi-minute 429 window
  (`:122-130`), so it is answered from the gauge and that window is never
  poked. Already pinned there by `provider-rate-limits.test.ts:710`, `:733` and
  `:798`.

Teaching the GUI to compute those floors would be the drift `semantics.ts`
exists to prevent, so it does not: the bound on ASKING is a flat 60s withhold
after a hand-driven read of one account settles, which is the shortest floor
that lane puts on an automatic read.

## What a person sees

- At rest: `Couldn't load, retrying`, dotted-underlined, tooltip
  `<provider> · Couldn't load, retrying - click to retry now`.
- While a read runs: `Retrying...`, no affordance - the read IS the retry.
- For 60s after a hand-driven retry settles: `Couldn't load, retrying`, no
  affordance.

Both sentences are true whenever they are up: the strip's poll keeps re-reading
these accounts on its own, every
`EPHEMERAL_RATE_LIMIT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (`rate-limit-timing.ts:7`, 15 minutes),
and its target filter is `usageUpdatedAt` alone -
`rate-limit-poll-targets.ts:73-82` never looks at `available`, so a
transient-failed account stays in the set, and `startVisibleInterval({
fireOnShow: true })` (`rate-limit-poll-provider.tsx:73-76`) ticks the moment the
window is shown, which is the moment a person can read the words.

The reason drops out of the TRANSIENT tooltip. `timeout`,
`connection_failed` and `usage_fetch_failed` differ in nothing the reader can
act on, and naming the mechanism is what the copy rule excludes. It stays on
the authoritative state, where it says what to fix.

## The click

A click on an offering segment does what a segment click already did - arms the
panel on that account's card (`statusBarSegmentAtClick`) - and reads that
account on the way in. The deep link is kept rather than replaced: the panel's
card is where the reading lands, and one gesture meaning two things on one
state would be worse. Mouse only, exactly as that deep link already is; the
keyboard opens the panel, whose per-account control is the retry there
(`:174-175` documented this before this change).

Lane routing is `useProviderRateLimitRefresh`'s, applied to a segment, and it
is the FORCED read's: `fetchProviderRateLimits` for `ephemeralProcess`, the
account's own observer refetch for `httpFetch`. `httpRefetches` is keyed by
account for that, so one segment's retry cannot refetch every http account the
strip holds. An unforced read takes neither path - see the re-read's own
bullet below.

Only a placement whose click actually reads offers one. `retryHostId` is a
required input of the hook, and a placement that passes `null` keeps the words
and drops the affordance: the header glyph, the header popover and the
layout-editor inspector all pass `null`, because their click opens the panel
and reads nothing. The status-bar cluster passes the strip's host id and is the
one placement that wires the forced read and the 60s re-read.

## Where the bounds live

- The 60s re-read asks through `collectProviderRateLimits` on BOTH lanes, the
  named path for a read the renderer's own freshness guard must not answer. It
  keeps `force: false` on the wire, so the host's floors still decide; it
  only declines to be short-circuited by the five-minute
  `PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITS_STALE_TIME_MS` window, which the failing read itself
  had just populated. The poll's own unforced reads are NOT this path: they go
  through `fetchProviderRateLimits` and keep the renderer's guard, which is
  what holds them to four wire reads an hour per window per stale account.
- The withhold after a hand-driven retry is a stamp in
  `rate-limit-read-ledger.ts`, written to `localStorage` when the forced read
  settles. That is the one layer every window of this app shares and the only
  one that survives a remount and a reload, so the bound cannot be lifted by
  hiding the strip, opening a second window or reloading. It is keyed by host,
  provider and profile, read against the strip's 60s sampled clock, and an
  unparsable stamp reads as absent. The ledger's own map is the floor under
  it: it holds in this window whatever storage does, so a refused write
  cannot leave a settled read unbounded, and a reader takes the more recent of
  the two. A stamp more than the withhold AHEAD of the clock is invalid and
  reads as absent, which is what a wall clock corrected backwards leaves
  behind; it is dropped rather than clamped to the present, since a clamp
  re-dates it on every read.
- The bound is READ at the click, not only where the affordance was drawn: an
  offer on screen is as current as the render that drew it, and a sibling
  window's read can settle in between. Mounted readers observe the stamps
  through the ledger's subscription - the `storage` event for a write they did
  not make, its own notification for one they did - so a refused offer stops
  inviting the click at once.
- The scheduled re-read is ONE per transient EPISODE - the whole run of
  failures - and the ledger is what remembers it, keyed the same way. The
  episode is IDENTIFIED by the envelope's `episode`, a value
  `buildProviderRateLimitEnvelope` mints from a counter on a reading and on an
  authoritative reason - the two answers about an account - and carries over
  every transient failure. One run of failures shares one value and no two runs
  share one, so an entry recording which episode spent the read answers "is one
  owed" by comparison, and nothing has to witness the answer that ended an
  episode. That matters because the answer usually lands where no strip is
  drawing the account: a background poll, a hidden window, a provider nobody
  has picked. One failure does start a run of its own: one that came back under
  a different credential than the attempt before it, which OpenCode is the
  provider that says. The run before it describes a credential this account no
  longer uses, and so does the read that run has already spent. The envelope
  REMEMBERS that credential (`credentialGeneration`), rather than reading it
  back off the two snapshot arms: a failure may omit the generation, and doing
  so replaces `latest` and clears `lastGood`, so after one of those the arms
  know nothing and the rotation behind it would be invisible.
- It is a counter and not a clock reading, deliberately. Two answers can share
  a millisecond, and a wall clock corrected backwards can date an answer where
  it has already dated one - either of which makes two runs look like a single
  run, and the second run then says `Couldn't load, retrying` for the length of
  the poll interval without retrying. A counter cannot, and nothing needs it to
  persist: no envelope persists either, so a reload starts every key cold and
  every identity fresh together. The times stay in `lastGoodAt` and
  `lastFailureAt`, where they were.
- The strip's timer spends the one-shot when it fires, the hook stops listing
  an account that has spent this episode's, and the timer's own key carries the
  episode. So a run that ends and begins again between two commits - an answer
  and the failure after it settling in one batch - gets its own full delay
  rather than firing on the previous run's deadline. A remount, a hidden usage
  region, a provider hidden in the arrangement, a profile the selection stops
  showing and a read starting and failing all leave the episode where it was;
  the 15-minute poll owns the cadence from the first re-read on.
- An entry's LIFE follows the account's existence, read from the host's own
  account inventory - `providers.list`, before eligibility, before the cache
  and before every display rule - and nothing on screen. Not the list this
  hook is handed either: that one is the display projection, and a provider
  leaves it for reasons that are not an account ceasing to exist (one OpenCode
  account answering `rate_limits_not_available` takes the whole provider out of
  it, siblings included). The display filter, the selection, the layout editor
  and the sample scene are all read out of it, because each of them hides an
  account that exists and is failing. Whether that list is the
  host's ANSWER is a question the list cannot answer - an unanswered query and
  a host with nothing left are both no providers - so the provider query's own
  settled state is what decides: an answered inventory prunes whatever it does
  not list, empty included, and silence prunes nothing. Entries of a
  host the strip is pointed away from are left where they are - that run of
  failures is still the run it was in, and dropping them is what would hand it
  a second read - and a cap with oldest-first eviction is what bounds those:
  an eviction costs at most one extra unforced read, which the host's floor
  bounds in turn.
- That record is in memory and not in storage, deliberately: it says what THIS
  renderer owes and has taken, and a sibling window with its own cache and its
  own poll must not be talked out of its first re-read. What bounds the
  provider traffic when two windows do act is the host's own floor, measured
  from the last ATTEMPT for that account scope, and it is NOT one number:
  - `ephemeralProcess` (codex, claude-code, grok): an unforced read inside
    `EPHEMERAL_RATE_LIMIT_READ_COOLDOWN_MS` of the last attempt is answered
    from the gauge, so any number of windows asking at once costs at most one
    probe per account per 60s. A Claude `usage_fetch_failed` sits in
    `RATE_LIMIT_PENALTY_COOLDOWN_MS` instead, 15 minutes, so it costs none at
    all - that window is the reason the floor exists.
  - `httpFetch` (openrouter, kilocode, huggingface, opencode, cursor,
    antigravity): `HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_READ_COOLDOWN_MS`, 15s. The 60s between an
    episode's entry and its one re-read is already past it, so the floor is
    not what bounds this lane - one scheduled read per episode per window is,
    and the client-side bound that makes that true is the episode entry above.
    The lane did not even have the floor until this round: its scheduled read
    went out through an observer refetch, which sends no `force` at all, and
    an absent `force` is FORCED on the wire.
- A scheduled read whose account is already being read stands down instead of
  asking again: the read in flight IS the retry the words promise, and on the
  `httpFetch` lane asking again refetches that account's observer, which
  cancels the request in flight and would abort a person's own forced read.
- The re-read timeout and the component that owns it are keyed by host too, so
  pointing the strip at a second host clears the one host A was waiting on and
  starts B's from when B entered the state.

selected_prs.title: feat(protocol,gui-app,cli): a per-agent routing choice, wait it out here on a usage limit
selected_prs.body:
## Cause

A usage limit or error is routed by the device's fallback policy only. There is no way for one agent to say "wait for the reset on this account, do not switch harness, model or account", so an agent doing long-running work on a specific account is moved off it whenever the device has automatic routing on, and left with no wait at all when it is off.

## Change

Protocol (`@traycer/protocol`):

- Chat record: optional `routing: "policy" | "hold"`; an absent value reads as `policy`. The field is on the live record only. Every released `chat.subscribe` line freezes the record without it (`chatRecordSchemaPreRouting`), the unreleased 1.23 line and above carry it, and the checkpoint digests for those lines are re-minted. The epic schema surface fixture is regenerated (only the `routing` enum entries).
- `agent.configure@7.1`: a request-only minor adding `routing`. A 7.0 caller, or `null`, leaves the agent's choice alone (the 7.1 schema requires the key). 7.0 upgrades with `routing: null`; every downgrade path to an older MAJOR refuses a non-null `routing` with `DOWNGRADE_UNSUPPORTED` rather than dropping it. A same-major 7.0 host strips the field it does not know, so a caller that sends a non-null `routing` pins the 7.1 floor on the request (`requiredHostMethodVersion`) and is refused instead of silently losing the wait.
- `agent.create@3.1`: a request-only minor adding the same `routing` field with the same meaning (`null` is the default, `policy`). 3.0 upgrades with `routing: null`; the downgrades to 2.x and 1.x still refuse, as they already did for any 3.x request.

GUI: a tab context-menu setting, "On a usage limit or error", with "Follow the device routing" and "Wait it out here". It is offered only when the host's negotiated `agent.configure` is 7.1 or above and the chat has a persisted run tuple; the chat configures itself and restates its tuple as it stands, so only the routing moves.

CLI: `agent configure` and `agent create` send `routing: null` on the 7.1 and 3.1 lines. No GUI control at creation: the tab menu is the GUI surface.

The host half (storage, the arm decision, clone carry) is in the paired internal PR; this PR is the contract it builds on.

## Proof

- `protocol/src/persistence/epic/__tests__/chat-routing.test.ts`: record round trip, an absent value, an unknown value is refused.
- `protocol/src/host/agent/__tests__/agent-configure-routing.test.ts`: 7.0 to 7.1 upgrade, 7.1 to each older line, non-null `routing` refused on every downgrade, `null` accepted.
- `released-baseline-compat`, `chat-schema-checkpoints`, `subscribe-windowed-line`, `epic-schema-surface` compat suites green (`src/persistence src/host src/framework`: 9095 tests).
- `protocol/src/host/agent/__tests__/agent-create-routing.test.ts`: line 3.1, the 3.0 strip, 3.1 requires the key, the upgrade, the downgrades still refuse. Released wire shapes stay byte-identical (the released-baseline suites are unchanged and green).
- gui-app `chat-routing-menu.test.tsx`: the record round trip, the request the setting sends, the version gate and the two choices in the menu.
- `protocol-compat.yml` dispatched on this branch.
